title.en: God the Creator and the deniers

essay.en:
The surah opens with praise, and al-Mizan reads the whole chapter as one sustained case for tawhid: the human being has a Lord who is Lord of all the worlds, from whom everything begins and to whom it returns, and the surah came down at Mecca as a single piece [1]. Its first three verses lay out three orders in turn, the cosmos, the human being, and human action [1]. God is praised as the One who 'created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light,' which Tabrisi glosses as night and day, named in that order because darkness was created before light [3]. Then the verse turns: 'the faithless equate others with their Lord.'

'It is He who created you from clay' means Adam, from whom the rest descend [3], 'then ordained the term of your life.' God is next named as knowing the hidden and the open, for 'He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth' says not that He occupies a place, but that He is the One worshipped and alone in governing everywhere [4].

The passage now faces the deniers. No sign of their Lord reaches them, such as the splitting of the moon or the verses of the Quran, without their turning away [5]; and soon 'the news of what they have been deriding' will reach them as a warning [2]. God recalls the generations before them, whom He had made kings and given rain and rivers, then destroyed for their sins, an argument against those who deny the resurrection [6]. Even a written book they could touch, they would call plain magic; Tabrisi reports this was revealed about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and others who demanded a book carried by angels [7]. They ask for an angel, yet an angel sent down would settle the matter with no reprieve, and an angel messenger would still be made a man, since human sight cannot bear an angel's form [8]. Al-Qummi adds that the Prophet asked to be spared such signs in mercy for his people, and was granted intercession [22]. The passage closes by consoling him: messengers before him were mocked, and the mockery closed in on the mockers [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: نزلت الأنعام جملة واحدة ويشيعها سبعون ألف ملك لهم زجل بالتسبيح والتهليل والتكبير فمن قرأها سبحوا له إلى يوم القيامة
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: Al-Anaam was revealed all at once, and seventy thousand angels escort it, with a clamor of glorification, declaring God one and declaring Him greatest; whoever recites it, they glorify God for him until the Day of Resurrection.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنهّا ردّ على ثلاثة أصناف لما قال الحمد لله الذي خلق السَّماوات والأرض كان ردّاً على الدّهرية … وجعل الظّلمات والنّور فكان ردّاً على الثنويّة الذين قالوا إنّ النّور والظّلمة هما المدّبران … ثمّ الذين كفروا بربهّم يعدلون فكان ردّاً على مشركي العرب الذين قالوا إنّ أوثاننا آلهة

text.en: In a hadith on the revelation of this verse: it refutes three groups. 'All praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth' refutes the materialists; 'and made the darkness and the light' refutes the dualists who claimed light and darkness are the two governors; and 'yet the faithless equate others with their Lord' refutes the Arab idolaters.

narrations.speaker: Abdullah ibn Abbas
narrations.arabic: انتهى به جبرئيل إلى نهر يقال له: النور و هو قول الله عز و جل: { وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ وَٱلنُّورَ } … يا محمد، أنا المحمود و أنت محمد، شققت اسمك من اسمي … أني لم أبعث نبيا إلا جعلت له وزيرا، و أنك رسولي، و أن عليا وزيرك
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from al-A'mash, from Abaya ibn Rib'i, from Abdullah ibn Abbas

text.en: When the Prophet ascended, Gabriel brought him to a river called al-Nur - and that is God's words, 'and made the darkness and the light.' The Lord said: 'I am al-Mahmud and you are Muhammad; I split your name from Mine. I never sent a prophet without a minister; you are My messenger, and Ali is your minister.'

note.en: 'The specified term is with Him' points to two terms the Imams distinguish: one decreed and fixed, and one open to bada, which God advances or delays [25].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الأجل المقضي: هو المحتوم الذي قضاه الله و حتمه، و المسمى: هو الذي فيه البداء، يقدم ما يشاء، و يؤخر ما يشاء، و المحتوم ليس فيه تقديم و لا تأخير
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The decreed term is the inevitable one that God has decreed and made certain. The named term is the one in which there is bada: He brings forward what He wills and delays what He wills. The inevitable term admits no advancing and no delay.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هما أجلان: أجل محتوم، و أجل موقوف
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Hamran, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Asked about 'then ordained the term - the specified term is with Him,' he said: They are two terms, a decreed term and a suspended term.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كذلك هو في كل مكان … و لكن هو بائن من خلقه، محيط بما خلق علما و قدرة و إحاطة و سلطانا و ملكا
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Ja'far, who asked Abu Abdillah

text.en: So He is in every place - but He is distinct from His creation, encompassing what He created in knowledge, power, dominion and sovereignty.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لبسوا عليهم، لبس الله عليهم. فإن الله يقول { وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّا يَلْبِسُونَ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur

text.en: They confounded others, so God confounded them - for God says, 'and We would have confounded them just as they confound.'

perspectives.en: On 'a specified term is with Him' the two traditions read the pair of terms differently. The Imams take them as one decreed and inevitable term and one suspended term open to bada, in which God brings a thing forward or holds it back [25]. The leading Sunni commentators read the pair as fixed stages instead: al-Tabari takes the first term as the span from creation to death and the second as the span from death to resurrection [32], and Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Abbas that the first means death and the second the hereafter [41].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان غرض السورة هو توحيده تعالى بمعناه الأعم أعني أن للإِنسان رباً هو رب العالمين جميعاً منه يبدأ كل شيء وإليه ينتهي ويعود كل شيء

sources.gloss: An account of the surah's purpose: God's oneness in the broadest sense - that the human being has a Lord who is Lord of all the worlds, from whom everything begins and to whom everything returns.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: قوله تعالى { فسوف يأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزؤون } تخويف وإنذار

sources.gloss: His words 'soon there will come to them the news of what they have been deriding' are a threat and a warning.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { وجعل الظلمات والنور } يعني الليل والنهار عن السدي وجماعة من المفسرين … { هو الذي خلقكم من طين } يعني به آدم

sources.gloss: 'And made the darkness and the light' means night and day, according to al-Suddi and a group of commentators … 'It is He who created you from clay' refers to Adam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يكون معناه أن المعبود في السماوات وفي الأرض أو المنفرد بالتدبير في السماوات وفي الأرض يعلم سرَّكم وجهركم

sources.gloss: It means that the One worshipped in the heavens and the earth, or the One alone in governing them, knows your secret and your open.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { من آيات ربهم } أي من حججه وبيناته كانشقاق القمر وآيات القرآن وغير ذلك من المعجزات { إلاَّ كانوا عنها معرضين }

sources.gloss: 'From the signs of their Lord' means His proofs and clear signs, such as the splitting of the moon, the verses of the Quran and other miracles - 'but that they used to disregard it.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { مكناهم في الأرض ما لم نمكن لكم } معناه جعلناهم ملوكاً وأغنياء … وفي هذه الآية دلالة على وجوب التفكر والتدبر واحتجاج على منكري البعث

sources.gloss: 'Whom We had granted power in the land in respects that We did not grant you' means We made them kings and rich … and in this verse is proof of the duty to reflect and an argument against those who deny the resurrection.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: النزول: نزلت في نضر بن الحرث وعبد الله بن أبي أمية ونوفل بن خويلد قالوا يا محمد لن نؤمن لك حتى تأتينا بكتاب الله ومعه أربعة من الملائكة يشهدون عليه أنه من عند الله

sources.gloss: Occasion of revelation: it came down about al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, who said, 'O Muhammad, we will not believe you until you bring us a book from God with four angels bearing witness that it is from God.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { لجعلناه رجلاً } لأنهم لا يستطيعون أن يروا الملك في صورته لأن أعين الخلق تحار عن رؤية الملائكة إلا بعد التجسم بالأجسام الكثيفة ولذلك كانت الملائكة تأتي الأنبياء في صورة الإنس وكان جبرائيل يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صورة دحية الكلبي

sources.gloss: 'We would have surely made him a man,' because they cannot see an angel in its form - human eyes are dazzled by the sight of angels except when they take on dense bodies; so angels came to the prophets in human form, and Gabriel would come to the Prophet in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت الأنعام جملة واحدة ويشيعها سبعون ألف ملك لهم زجل بالتسبيح والتهليل والتكبير فمن قرأها سبحوا له إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: Al-Anaam was revealed all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels with a clamor of glorification; whoever recites it, they glorify God for him until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فاستعفى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله من الآيات رأفة ورحمة على أمته وأعطاه الله الشفاعة

sources.gloss: So the Prophet asked to be excused from the signs, out of tenderness and mercy for his community, and God granted him intercession.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: انتهى به جبرئيل إلى نهر يقال له: النور و هو قول الله عز و جل: { وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ وَٱلنُّورَ }

sources.gloss: Gabriel brought him to a river called al-Nur - and that is God's words, 'and made the darkness and the light.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الأجل المقضي: هو المحتوم الذي قضاه الله و حتمه، و المسمى: هو الذي فيه البداء، يقدم ما يشاء، و يؤخر ما يشاء

sources.gloss: The decreed term is the inevitable one that God has decreed and made certain; the named term is the one in which there is bada - He brings forward what He wills and delays what He wills.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كذلك هو في كل مكان … و لكن هو بائن من خلقه، محيط بما خلق علما و قدرة و إحاطة و سلطانا و ملكا

sources.gloss: So He is, in every place … but He is distinct from His creation, encompassing what He created in knowledge, power, dominion and sovereignty.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لبسوا عليهم، لبس الله عليهم. فإن الله يقول { وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّا يَلْبِسُونَ }

sources.gloss: They confounded others, so God confounded them - for God says, 'and We would have confounded them just as they confound.'

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في الإِحتجاج عن الصادق عليه السلام في حديث في نزول هذه الآية أنهّا ردّ على ثلاثة أصناف

sources.gloss: In al-Ihtijaj, from al-Sadiq, in a hadith on the revelation of this verse: that it is a refutation of three groups.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: معنى قوله: { ثُمَّ قَضَى أجَلاً }: ثم قضى لكم أيها الناس أجلاً، وذلك ما بين أن يُخلق إلى أن يموت وأجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ وذلك ما بين أن يموت إلى أن يبعث

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'then ordained a term' is: He decreed for you a term, that between being created and dying; and 'a specified term is with Him' is that between dying and being resurrected.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: قال سعيد بن جُبَير، عن ابن عباس { ثُمَّ قَضَىۤ أَجَلاً } ، يعني الموت، { وَأَجَلٌ مُّسمًّى عِندَهُ } يعني الآخرة

sources.gloss: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas: 'then ordained a term' means death, and 'a specified term is with Him' means the hereafter.

essay.en: The passage is a chain of 'Say' commands to the Prophet, pressing the case for God's oneness and the Resurrection against the Meccan idolaters. It opens by telling him to bid the deniers, 'Travel over the land, and then observe how was the fate of the deniers': the ruins of past nations still stood and their fate was known, so the journey would hold the doubters back from denial [9]. al-Mizan reads the destruction of those nations for their sins as a sign that wrongdoing has a share in the calamities that strike whole peoples [1]. Then comes a question and its own answer: 'To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?' 'To Allah.' al-Mizan takes this to open a proof of the Resurrection: the Owner of all things, who has 'made mercy incumbent upon Himself,' will surely gather everyone on a Day beyond doubt [2]. Tabrisi records the written mercy read as the respite God grants His servants so they may repent of what they neglected [4]. 'To Him belongs whatever abides in the night and the day' joins time to place: He made night and day a dwelling enclosing all they contain, so nothing created falls outside His ownership [10]. The commands turn next to guardianship: 'Shall I take for guardian anyone other than Allah, the originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed?' The Prophet is made to answer that he was commanded to be first among those who submit and never to join the idolaters, and that he fears 'a tremendous day' should he disobey his Lord. Whoever is spared that punishment on the Day has been shown mercy - the manifest success. No distress that God sends can be lifted by any but Him, and He is 'the All-dominant over His servants' - a dominance of overpowering and subjugation, not of place [7]. Finally the Prophet asks what is greatest as a witness and answers, 'Allah': the revealed Quran is itself God's testimony to the message, sent to warn Mecca and all it reaches, and he disowns every partner set beside the one God. Tabatabai reads this as an argument for God's oneness established by way of revelation [3]. It ends by turning to the People of the Book, who know him as surely as their own sons, yet those who have ruined their souls will not believe.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عنى بذلك أي انظروا في القرآن فاعلموا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلكم، و ما أخبركم عنه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Zayd ibn al-Walid al-Khath'ami, from Abu al-Rabi al-Shami

text.en: Al-Rabi al-Shami asked al-Sadiq about the like command to travel the land and observe the fate of those before them. He answered that it means: look into the Quran, and thereby learn how the end of those before you was, and what it reports to you of them.

note.en: Feeding is singled out because the servants' need of it is most pressing, and to deny it of God most clearly rules out any likeness between Him and creatures [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما ترك رسول الله صلىّ الله عليه وآله وسلم إنّي أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم حتى نزلت سورة الفتح فلم يعد الى ذلك الكلام

text.en: Al-Sadiq said the Messenger of God never ceased saying, 'Indeed, should I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of a tremendous day,' until Surah al-Fath was revealed; after that he did not return to those words.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: والذي نفسي بيده ما من الناس أحد يدخل الجنة بعمله … ولا أنا إلا أن يتغمَّدني الله برحمة منه وفضل

text.en: By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one among people enters Paradise by his deeds. They said, 'Not even you, Messenger of God?' He said, 'Not even I, unless God envelops me in mercy and grace from Him.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وذلك أن مشركي أهل مكة قالوا يا محمد ما وجد الله رسولاً يرسله غيرك، ما نرى أحداً يصدقك بالذي تقول … فتأتينا من يشهد أنك رسول الله، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: الله شهيد بيني وبينكم
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Al-Baqir said the Meccan idolaters told the Prophet: 'Muhammad, did God find no messenger to send but you? We see none believing what you say.' They asked him to bring someone to witness that he was God's messenger, so the Prophet said, 'Allah is witness between me and you.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من بلغ معناه من بلغ أن يكون إماماً من آل محمد فهو ينذر بالقرآن كما أنذر به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah

text.en: Al-Baqir and al-Sadiq explained 'and whomever it may reach' to mean: whoever reaches the rank of being an Imam from the family of Muhammad warns by the Quran, just as the Messenger of God warned by it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزلت هذه الآية في اليهود و النصارى … يعني رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) لأن الله جل و عز قد أنزل عليهم في التوراة و الإنجيل و الزبور صفة محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) و صفة أصحابه و مبعثه و مهاجره
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Hurayz, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Al-Sadiq said this verse was revealed about the Jews and Christians. They know him as they know their sons, meaning the Messenger of God, because God had set down for them in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms the description of Muhammad, of his companions, and of his migration.

perspectives.en: On 'and whomever it may reach' (verse 19), the two traditions parse 'man balagha' differently. Tabari takes it as the object of the warning: the Prophet warns by the Quran everyone it reaches, of all people besides the Meccans it first addressed [36]. Tabrisi reports from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq a reading that instead takes the phrase in the nominative, as the one who reaches: whoever attains the rank of being an Imam from the family of Muhammad warns by the Quran, just as the Messenger warned by it. On that reading it is joined to the subject who warns, not to those warned [8].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفي قوله { فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم } دلالة على أن للسيئات والذنوب دخلاً في البلايا والمحن العامة

sources.gloss: In His words 'so We destroyed them for their sins' is proof that sins have a part in the general calamities and afflictions.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: شروع في البرهنة على المعاد، ومحصله أن الله تعالى مالك ما في السماوات والأرض جميعاً له أن يتصرف فيها كيف شاء وأراد

sources.gloss: This begins the proof of the Return: its gist is that God owns all that is in the heavens and the earth and may dispose of it however He wills.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: احتجاج على الوحدانية من طريق الوحي

sources.gloss: An argument for God's oneness by way of revelation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أوجب على نفسه الرحمة بأنظاره عباده وإمهاله إياهم ليتداركوا ما فرطوا فيه ويتوبوا عن معاصيهم

sources.gloss: He made mercy binding on Himself by granting His servants respite and delay, so they may make up what they neglected and repent of their sins.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: إنما ذكر الإطعام لأن حاجة العباد إليه أشَدّ ولأنّ نفيه عن الله أدلّ على نفي شبهه بالمخلوقين

sources.gloss: Feeding is mentioned because the servants' need of it is most pressing, and denying it of God most clearly denies any likeness between Him and creatures.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ما من الناس أحد يدخل الجنة بعمله

sources.gloss: No one among people enters Paradise by his deeds.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: معنى فوق ها هنا قهره واستعلاؤه عليهم فهم تحت تسخيره وتذليله

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'above' here is His overpowering and elevation over them, so that they are under His subjugation and subdual.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: من بلغ معناه من بلغ أن يكون إماماً من آل محمد فهو ينذر بالقرآن كما أنذر به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم … وعلى هذا فيكون قولـه ومن بلغ في موضع رفع عطفاً على الضمير في أنذر

sources.gloss: 'And whoever reaches' means: whoever reaches the rank of being an Imam from the family of Muhammad warns by the Quran as the Messenger of God warned by it; and on this reading His words 'and whoever reaches' are in the nominative, conjoined to the subject in 'that I may warn.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ان يسيروا في الارض لينظروا الى آثار تلك الامم فانها مشهورة ومتواتر خبرها معلوم مساكنها واراد بذلك زجر هؤلاء الكفار عن تكذيب محمد

sources.gloss: That they travel the land to look at the traces of those nations, for they are well known and their reports widely transmitted, their dwellings known; by this He meant to restrain these disbelievers from denying Muhammad.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أي ما اشتمل عليه الليل والنهار فجعل الليل والنهار كالمسكن لما اشتملا عليه

sources.gloss: Meaning what the night and the day contain; He made the night and day like a dwelling for what they enclose.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وذلك أن مشركي أهل مكة قالوا يا محمد ما وجد الله رسولاً يرسله غيرك

sources.gloss: This is because the idolaters of Mecca said: 'Muhammad, God found no messenger to send but you?'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عنى بذلك أي انظروا في القرآن فاعلموا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلكم

sources.gloss: He meant by that: look into the Quran, and learn how the fate of those before you was.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزلت هذه الآية في اليهود و النصارى

sources.gloss: This verse was revealed about the Jews and the Christians.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ما ترك رسول الله صلىّ الله عليه وآله وسلم إنّي أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم حتى نزلت سورة الفتح

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God did not cease saying 'I fear, should I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day,' until Surah al-Fath was revealed.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وأنذر به من بلغه من سائر الناس غيركم

sources.gloss: And warn by it whomever it reaches of all people besides you.

essay.en:
The passage opens by naming the worst of all wrongs: 'Who is a greater wrongdoer than him who fabricates a lie against Allah, or denies His signs?' Tabatabai reads wrongdoing as the most heinous of sins, and the wronging of God's own sacred precinct - by inventing partners for Him or rejecting His signs - as the gravest of all; the verse fits the idol-worshippers, who set up their idols as intercessors. [1] Tusi adds that such a man wrongs and destroys only himself. [8]

On the day of gathering God asks the polytheists, 'Where are your partners that you used to claim?' Their only plea is to swear, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.' Tabrisi records a report from Muqatil that, seeing God pardon the people of monotheism, they had urged one another to profess monotheism and so escape. [2] They lie against themselves, and what they fabricated deserts them.

Some of them listen to the Prophet yet grasp nothing, for veils lie on their hearts and deafness in their ears, and they dismiss the recitation as 'myths of the ancients.' Tabrisi records a report that the verse came down over al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and other Meccan chiefs who sat listening and then mocked. [4] They turn others away from the Prophet and keep away themselves, ruining no one but themselves.

Were you to see them halted at the Fire, they beg to be sent back to believe; but the wish is not sincere, and were they returned they would revert. They had said there is nothing but this world, and no resurrection. Yet halted before their Lord and asked, 'Is this not a fact?', they swear, 'Yes, by our Lord!' Tusi warns that being brought to a halt before their Lord is not a seeing of God, as the anthropomorphists claimed, but a halting before His reckoning. [15] In the end the denier is condemned by his own tongue.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: قوله عز و جل: { وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ }. قال: يعنون بولاية علي (عليه السلام)
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Regarding God's words, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists' - they mean by this the wilayah of Ali.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله يعفو يوم القيامة عفوا لا يخطر على بال أحد، حتى يقول أهل الشرك { وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God will pardon on the Day of Resurrection with a pardon that never crossed anyone's mind, until the people of shirk say, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: قوله تعالى: { وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذْ وُقِفُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ فَقَالُواْ يٰلَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَٰتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ } نزلت في بني أمية

text.en: 'Were you to see when they are brought to a halt by the Fire' and beg to be sent back to believe - this was revealed about Banu Umayya.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: { بل بدا لهم ما كانوا يخفون من قبل } قال: من عداوة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

text.en: 'Indeed, what they used to hide before has now become evident to them' - namely, their enmity toward the Commander of the Faithful.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: { وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ لَعَادُواْ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنْهُ } إنهم ملعونون في الأصل
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Khalid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: 'But were they to be sent back, they would revert to what they were forbidden' - they are cursed at their root.

perspectives.en: On 'they dissuade others from him and keep away from him,' the traditions divide over Abu Talib. Tusi and Tabrisi refer the verse to the obstinate Quraysh and reject applying it to Abu Talib, holding his faith proven by the consensus of the Ahl al-Bayt and by his own well-known poetry. [12][5] Several Sunni reports, gathered by al-Suyuti from Ibn Abbas, instead apply it to Abu Talib himself - that he shielded the Prophet from harm yet kept away from what he brought - and al-Qurtubi transmits a tradition that his punishment in the Fire was only lightened, not lifted. [63][48]

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الظلم من أشنع الذنوب

sources.gloss: Wrongdoing is among the most heinous of sins.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل إن المشركين إذا رأوا تجاوز الله تعالى عن أهل التوحيد قال بعضهم لبعض إذا سئلتم فقولوا إنا موحّدون فلما جمعهم الله قال لهم أين شركاؤكم ليعلموا أن الله يعرف أنهم أشركوا به في دار الدنيا وأنه لا ينفعهم الكتمان عن مقاتل

sources.gloss: It is said that when the polytheists saw God pass over the people of monotheism, they said to one another, 'If you are questioned, say we are monotheists'; so when God gathered them He asked, 'Where are your partners?' - so they would know that concealment does not help them; from Muqatil.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل إن نفراً من مشركي مكة منهم النضر بن الحارث وأبو سفيان بن حرب والوليد بن المغيرة وعتبة بن ربيعة وأخوه شيبة وغيرهم جلسوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يقرأ القرآن فقالوا للنضر: ما يقول محمد فقال أساطير الأولين

sources.gloss: It is said that a group of Meccan polytheists - among them al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu Sufyan, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Utbah and his brother Shaybah, and others - sat by the Messenger while he recited, and asked al-Nadr what Muhammad was saying; he said, 'myths of the ancients.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقد ثبت إجماع أهل البيت ع على إيمان أبي طالب وإجماعهم حجة

sources.gloss: The consensus of the Ahl al-Bayt on the faith of Abu Talib is established, and their consensus is a proof.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لا أحد أظلم لنفسه منه اذ كان بهذا الفعل قد أهلك نفسه

sources.gloss: No one wrongs himself more than he, for by this act he has destroyed himself.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل: نزلت في أبي طالب، وهذا باطل عندنا، لانه دل الدليل على إِيمانه بما ثبت عنه من شعره المعروف

sources.gloss: It is said it was revealed about Abu Talib, but this is false in our view, for the evidence of his faith is established by his well-known poetry.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقد ظن قوم من المشبهة أن قوله { إذ وقفوا على ربهم } أنهم يشاهدونه، وهذا فاسد

sources.gloss: Some anthropomorphists supposed that 'when they are brought to a halt before their Lord' means they behold Him; but this is false.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: من عداوة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

sources.gloss: From enmity toward the Commander of the Faithful.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قوله عز و جل: { وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ } قال: يعنون بولاية علي (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: His words 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists' - he said, they mean by it the wilayah of Ali.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: { وَلَوْ رُدُّواْ لَعَادُواْ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنْهُ } إنهم ملعونون في الأصل

sources.gloss: 'Were they returned they would revert to what they were forbidden' - they are cursed at their root.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: إنما عذابه في نعلين من نار في رجليه يغلي منهما دماغه في رأسه وذلك أهون أهل النار عذاباً

sources.gloss: His punishment is only two sandals of fire on his feet from which his brain boils, and that is the lightest punishment of the people of the Fire.

sources.author: Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti

excerpt.text: نزلت في أبي طالب، كان ينهى المشركين أن يؤذوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويتباعد عما جاء به

sources.gloss: It was revealed about Abu Talib; he used to forbid the polytheists from harming the Messenger of God and kept away from what he brought.

essay.en:
The passage turns back to address the Prophet directly, setting out the wrongs the idolaters commit against the three foundations of true belief: God's oneness, prophethood, and the resurrection [1]. It opens on the losers who deny 'the encounter with Allah,' which Tusi reads as the reckoning of reward and punishment God has promised, named a meeting with Him [9]. When the Hour overtakes them suddenly they cry, 'Alas for us,' bent under the burdens on their backs. Against this, 'the life of the world is nothing but play and diversion,' its pleasures passing and leaving no trace, while the abode of the Hereafter is better for the Godwary [10].

God then consoles His Messenger: their words grieve you, yet it is not you they deny. Tabatabai notes that the verse turns from 'them' to 'the wrongdoers' to show their rejection springs from wrongdoing, not from ignorance; it is sheer defiance [2]. Apostles before him were denied and bore it patiently until God's help came, and nothing can change the words of God. If their aversion weighs on him, could he seek a tunnel into the ground or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign? Had God wished, He would have brought them together on guidance, but only by compulsion, which He declined, since forcing faith would empty the trial of its worth [6].

Only those who truly listen respond; the rest are as the dead. They demand a sign from his Lord, though the Quran, the greatest of signs, was already before them and they refused to count it as one [3]. Every animal on land and bird in the air, the passage adds, is a community like their own, and nothing has been left out of the Book. Those who deny are deaf and dumb, lost in a manifold darkness. It closes with a challenge: when God's punishment or the Hour strikes, will they call on any but Him? No, Him alone they will call, and they will forget the partners they ascribed to Him.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: يرى أهل النار منازلهم من الجنة، فيقولون: يا حسرتنا
narrations.chain: al-Tabrisi, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Said, from the Prophet

text.en: The people of the Fire will see their places in Paradise and will cry, 'Alas for us!'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: يا هشام، ثم وعظ أهل العقل و رغبهم في الآخرة، فقال … وَمَا ٱلْحَيَٰوةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلاَّ لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَلَلدَّارُ ٱلآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ أَفَلاَ تَعْقِلُونَ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah al-Ashari, from one of our companions, raising it, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam

text.en: O Hisham, He then admonished the people of reason and made them long for the Hereafter, saying: 'The life of the world is nothing but play and diversion, and the abode of the Hereafter is surely better for those who are Godwary. Do you not exercise your reason?'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: بلى و الله لقد كذبوه أشد التكذيب، و لكنها مخففة: لا يكذبونك، أي لا يأتون بباطل يكذبون به حقك
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saad, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, from Imran ibn Maytham, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Yes, by God, they denied him most severely; but it is read lightened, 'la yukdhibunaka,' meaning they bring no falsehood by which to refute your truth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يَا حَفْصُ إِنَّ مَنْ صَبَرَ صَبَرَ قَلِيلاً وَإِنَّ مَنْ جَزِعَ جَزِعَ قَلِيلاً ثُمَّ قَالَ عَلَيْكَ بِالصَّبْرِ فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِكَ … الصَّبْرُ مِنَ الإيمَانِ كَالرَّأْسِ مِنَ الْجَسَدِ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, both from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Asbahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath

text.en: O Hafs, whoever is patient is patient only a little, and whoever is anxious is anxious only a little. Hold to patience in all your affairs. God sent Muhammad and commanded him with patience and gentleness. Patience is to faith as the head is to the body.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يحب إسلام الحارث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف، دعاه رسول الله … و جهد به أن يسلم، فغلب عليه الشقاء
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The Messenger of Allah longed for al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal to embrace Islam, and the Messenger called him and strove hard with him to submit, but wretchedness overcame him. That weighed on the Messenger of Allah, so God revealed, 'And should their aversion be hard on you.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: و سيريكم في آخر الزمان آيات، منها: دابة الأرض، و الدجال، و نزول عيسى بن مريم … و طلوع الشمس من مغربها
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, in the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He will show you signs at the end of time: among them the beast of the earth, the Dajjal, the descent of Jesus son of Mary, and the rising of the sun from its place of setting.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل لم يقبض نبينا … حتى أكمل له الدين، و أنزل عليه القرآن فيه تبيان كل شيء، بين فيه الحلال و الحرام، و الحدود و الأحكام، و جميع ما يحتاج إليه الناس كملا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu Muhammad al-Qasim ibn al-Ala, raising it, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, from al-Rida

text.en: God did not take our Prophet until He had perfected the religion for him and sent down the Quran, in which is the exposition of everything: the lawful and the unlawful, the limits and the rulings, and all that people need, in full.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزلت في الذين كذبوا بأوصيائهم، صم بكم، كما قال الله في الظلمات، من كان من ولد إبليس فإنه لا يصدق بالأوصياء ولا يؤمن بهم أبداً وهم الذين أضلهم الله، ومن كان من ولد آدم آمن بالأوصياء فهم على صراط مستقيم
narrations.chain: Jafar ibn Ahmad, from Abd al-Karim, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza

text.en: It was revealed about those who denied their successors: deaf and dumb, as God said, in darkness. Whoever is of the offspring of Iblis never affirms the successors and never believes in them; they are the ones God has led astray. Whoever is of the offspring of Adam believes in the successors; they are on a straight path.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا عبد الله هل ركبت سفينة قط؟ قال: نعم قال: فهل كسر بك حيث لا سفينة تنجيك ولا سباحة تغنيك؟ قال: نعم … فذلك الشئ هو الله القادر على الانجاء حيث لا منجي، وعلى الإغاثة حيث لا مغيث

text.en: O servant of God, have you ever boarded a ship? Yes. Has it been wrecked where no ship could save you and no swimming avail you? Yes. Did your heart cling then to something able to deliver you? Yes. That thing is God, who rescues when there is no rescuer and aids when there is no aider.

perspectives.en: Verses 35 and 39 divide the commentators over free will. Al-Razi takes 'Had Allah wished, He would have brought them together on guidance' to mean God does not will the disbeliever's faith but wills to keep him upon disbelief, and reads 'Allah leads astray whomever He wishes' as proof that guidance and misguidance belong to God alone [63][67]. Tusi reads the same words the other way: God only declined to compel faith, which would void moral accountability and its reward, so the choice stays the person's; and to be 'led astray' is His forsaking of those who turn from the evidence, never the prophets or believers [13][17].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: تعود الآيات إلى أصل السياق وهو الحضور فتلتفت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالخطاب فتذكر له مظالم المشركين في أُصول العقائد الطاهرة وهي التوحيد والاعتقاد بالنبوة والمعاد

sources.gloss: The verses return to the main address, turning to the Prophet and recounting to him the polytheists' wrongs in the pure foundations of belief: God's oneness, faith in prophethood, and the resurrection.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالعدول إلى الظاهر للدلالة على أن الجحد منهم إنما هو عن ظلم منهم لا عن قصور وجهل وغير ذلك فليس إلا عتواً وبغياً وطغياناً

sources.gloss: The switch to the plain word 'the wrongdoers' shows their rejection comes from their own wrongdoing, not from any deficiency or ignorance; it is nothing but insolence, transgression, and rebellion.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولما صدر هذا القول منهم وبين أيديهم أفضل الآيات أعني القرآن الكريم الذي كان ينزل عليهم سورة سورة وآية آية

sources.gloss: They said this while the best of signs, the Noble Quran, was before them, coming down to them sura by sura and verse by verse.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: بالإِلجاء وإنما أخبر عز اسمه عن كمال قدرته وأنه لو شاء لأَلجأهم إلى الإِيمان ولم يفعل ذلك لأَنه ينافي التكليف ويسقط استحقاق الثواب

sources.gloss: By compulsion He could have gathered them; He tells of His full power to compel them to faith, yet did not do so, for that would nullify moral responsibility and forfeit the reward.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الذين كذبوا بما وعد الله به من الثواب والعقاب وجعل لقاءهم لذلك لقاء له تعالى مجازا

sources.gloss: Those who denied the reward and punishment God promised; their meeting with that is called, figuratively, a meeting with Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أن ما يتمتع به في الدنيا بمنزلة اللعب واللهو، اللذين لا عاقبة لهما في المنفعة ويقتضي زوالهما عن أهلها في أدنى مدة وأسرع زمان، لانه لا ثبات لهما ولا بقاء

sources.gloss: What one enjoys in the world is like play and diversion, which bring no lasting benefit and pass from their people in the briefest span, for they have no permanence.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وانما أفاد نفي المشيئة لما يلجئهم الى الايمان، لانه متى ألجأهم اليه لم يكن ذلك ايمانا يستحق عليه الثواب

sources.gloss: The verse only denies the will to compel them to faith, for once He compelled them it would no longer be a faith deserving reward.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لا يجوز ان يكون على عمومه، لانا قد علمنا ان الله تعالى لا يشاء ان يضل الانبياء والمؤمنين ولا يهدي الكافرين

sources.gloss: It cannot be taken in a general sense, for we know God does not will to lead the prophets and believers astray, nor to guide the disbelievers.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت في الذين كذبوا بأوصيائهم، صم بكم، كما قال الله في الظلمات، من كان من ولد إبليس فإنه لا يصدق بالأوصياء ولا يؤمن بهم أبداً وهم الذين أضلهم الله، ومن كان من ولد آدم آمن بالأوصياء فهم على صراط مستقيم

sources.gloss: It was revealed about those who denied their successors: deaf and dumb, in darkness. Whoever is of Iblis's offspring never affirms the successors; they are the ones God led astray. Whoever is of Adam's offspring believes in them; they are on a straight path.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يرى أهل النار منازلهم من الجنة، فيقولون: يا حسرتنا

sources.gloss: The people of the Fire will see their places in Paradise and say, 'Alas for us!'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يا هشام، ثم وعظ أهل العقل و رغبهم في الآخرة، فقال

sources.gloss: O Hisham, then He admonished the people of reason and made them long for the Hereafter, and cited this verse.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: بلى و الله لقد كذبوه أشد التكذيب، و لكنها مخففة: لا يكذبونك، أي لا يأتون بباطل يكذبون به حقك

sources.gloss: Yes, by God, they denied him most severely; but it is read lightened, 'la yukdhibunaka,' meaning they bring no falsehood by which to refute your truth.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يحب إسلام الحارث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف، دعاه رسول الله

sources.gloss: The Messenger of Allah longed for al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal to embrace Islam and called him to it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: حتى أكمل له الدين، و أنزل عليه القرآن فيه تبيان كل شيء، بين فيه الحلال و الحرام، و الحدود و الأحكام، و جميع ما يحتاج إليه الناس كملا

sources.gloss: God perfected the religion for the Prophet and sent down the Quran, containing the exposition of everything: the lawful and unlawful, the limits and the rulings, and all that people need, in full.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وذلك يدل على أنه تعالى لا يريد الإيمان من الكافر بل يريد إبقاءه على الكفر

sources.gloss: This shows that God does not will faith from the disbeliever but wills to keep him upon disbelief.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: احتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن الهدى والضلال ليس إلا من الله تعالى

sources.gloss: Our colleagues have argued from this verse that guidance and misguidance are from none but God.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: يَا حَفْصُ إِنَّ مَنْ صَبَرَ صَبَرَ قَلِيلاً وَإِنَّ مَنْ جَزِعَ جَزِعَ قَلِيلاً ثُمَّ قَالَ عَلَيْكَ بِالصَّبْرِ فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِكَ

sources.gloss: O Hafs, whoever is patient is patient only a little, and whoever is anxious is anxious only a little. Hold to patience in all your affairs.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: فذلك الشئ هو الله القادر على الانجاء حيث لا منجي، وعلى الإغاثة حيث لا مغيث

sources.gloss: That thing is God, able to rescue when there is no rescuer and to aid when there is no aider.

essay.en:
The passage recalls how God has dealt with rejecting nations, then turns those dealings into an argument against the Meccans and closes with the Prophet naming his own limits. Al-Mizan reads the whole section as varied arguments against the polytheists over God's oneness and the sign of prophethood [1]. It opens by reminding the Prophet that God sent apostles to nations before him and then gripped them with hardship and pain so that they might humble themselves and entreat Him; Tabrisi notes this serves as a consolation to the Prophet, whose own people were doing the same [2].

When the punishment came they still did not entreat: their hearts had hardened and Satan dressed up their deeds. Tusi stresses that it is Satan, not God, who makes disbelief seem fair to the disbeliever [5]. Then, when they forgot the warning, God opened to them the gates of all things - wide provision offered as a trial, not a favor [6]. Al-Safi cites the Prophet: if you see God bestowing on the sinner, that is a gradual enticement [22]. When they exulted, He seized them suddenly and they despaired, and the wrongdoers were rooted out.

The dealings now become proof: if God took your hearing and sight and sealed your hearts, which god but He could return them? Tabrisi observes these faculties are named because through them blessing is completed in faith and in worldly life [3]. If His punishment came suddenly or openly, only the wrongdoers are destroyed; Tusi adds that if believers or children perish, it is a trial for which God repays them [8]. The messengers were sent only as bearers of good news and warners, not as lords who can produce any sign demanded [9]. Finally the Prophet disclaims God's treasuries, knowledge of the Unseen, and being an angel; Tusi notes he was told to say this so that none would exalt him as the Christians exalted the Messiah [10]. Are the blind and the seeing equal? In the reading of the Ahl al-Bayt: the one who knows and the one who does not [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أما قوله: { فلما نسوا ما ذكروا به } يعني: فلما تركوا ولاية علي أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام وقد أمروا به { فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء } يعني دولتهم في الدنيا وما بسط لهم فيها وأما قوله: { حتى إذا فرحوا بما أوتوا أخذناهم بغتة فإذا هم مبلسون } يعني بذلك قيام القائم حتى كانهم لم يكن لهم سلطان قط، فذلك قوله بغتة
narrations.chain: Jafar ibn Ahmad, from Abd al-Karim ibn Abd al-Rahim, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'When they forgot what they had been reminded of' means they abandoned the wilaya of Ali, Commander of the Faithful, which they had been commanded to keep. 'We opened for them the gates of all things' is their worldly dynasty; 'We seized them suddenly' is the rising of the Qa'im, as if they never held power.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا موسى إذا رأيت الفقر مقبلاً فقل مرحباً بشعار الصالحين، وإذا رأيت الغنى مقبلاً فقل ذنب عجلت عقوبته، فما فتح الله على أحد هذه الدنيا إلا بذنب لينسيه ذلك فلا يتوب فيكون إقبال الدنيا عليه عقوبة لذنوبه.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God's whispered counsel to Musa was: O Musa, when you see poverty approaching, say 'Welcome, mark of the righteous.' When you see wealth approaching, say 'A sin whose punishment has been hastened.' God opens this world to no one except through a sin, to make him forget and not repent, so its coming becomes a punishment.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ومن أحب أن يعصي الله فقد بارز الله بالعداوة ومن أحب بقاء الظالمين فقد أحب أن يعصي الله إن الله تبارك وتعالى حمد نفسه على هلاك الظالمين قال: { فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين }.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Whoever loves the survival of the wrongdoers has loved that God be disobeyed. Indeed God praised Himself for the destruction of the wrongdoers, saying: 'Thus the wrongdoing lot were rooted out, and all praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يقول: إن أخذ الله منكم الهدى { مَّنْ إِلَـٰهٌ غَيْرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ ٱنْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ ثُمَّ هُمْ يَصْدِفُونَ } يقول: يعرضون
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He says: if God took away from you the guidance - 'which god other than Allah can bring it back to you? Look, how We paraphrase the signs variously; nevertheless they turn away' - meaning they turn aside.

note.en: Al-Qummi relates that this verse came when the Muhajirun, worn by hardship and illness at Medina, complained to the Prophet: worldly hardship touches everyone, but the destroying punishment falls only on the wrongdoers [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لما صعد موسى على نبيّنا وآله وعليه السلام إلى الطّور فنادى ربّه عزّ وجلّ قال يا ربّ أرني خزائنك فقال تعالى يا موسى إنّما خزائني إذا أردت شيئاً أن أقول له كن فيكون

text.en: When Musa ascended the Mount and called upon his Lord, he said: O Lord, show me Your treasuries. God said: O Musa, My treasuries are only that when I will a thing, I say to it 'Be,' and it is.

perspectives.en: These verses became a battleground over free will. Reading verse 43, Tusi says the text shows that Satan, not God, makes disbelief attractive, and that God genuinely willed the disbelievers' faith [5]; on verse 46 he adds that God enabled them to respond and did not create their turning away [7]. Razi, the Ash'ari, reads the same verses to the opposite end: verse 43 proves that whomever God does not guide is not guided [43], and verse 46 shows that guidance and misguidance come about only by God's guiding and leading astray [45].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان احتجاجات متنوعة على المشركين في أمر التوحيد وآية النبوة

sources.gloss: A setting out of various arguments against the polytheists concerning God's oneness and the sign of prophethood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذا كالتسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: And this serves as a consolation to the Prophet.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإنما خصّ هذه الأشياء بالذكر لأن بها تتم النعمة ديناً ودنيا

sources.gloss: These things were singled out for mention because through them the blessing is completed, in religion and in worldly life.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي تفسير أهل البيت هل يستوي من يعلم ومن لا يعلم

sources.gloss: In the interpretation of the Ahl al-Bayt: are the one who knows and the one who does not know equal?

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقد اخبر الله في هذه الآية ان الشيطان هو الذي يزين الكفر للكافر بخلاف ما يقول المجبرة من ان الله هو المزين لهم ذلك

sources.gloss: God has declared in this verse that it is Satan who makes disbelief seem fair to the disbeliever, contrary to the predestinarians who say God is the one who adorns it for them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ابتليناهم بالتوسعة في الرزق ليرغبوا بذلك في نعيم الآخرة

sources.gloss: We tried them with expansion in provision so that they might thereby desire the bliss of the Hereafter.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دليل على ان الله قد مكنهم من الاقبال على ما ورد عليهم من البيان وانه لم يخلق فيهم الاعراض عنه

sources.gloss: In the verse is proof that God enabled them to turn toward the exposition that came to them, and that He did not create in them the turning away.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومتى هلك فيهم اطفال او قوم مؤمنون فانما يهلكون امتحانا ويعوضهم الله على ذلك أعواضا كثيرة

sources.gloss: If children or believers perish among them, they perish only as a trial, and God compensates them for that with abundant recompense.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انه لا يبعث الرسل أربابا يقدرون على كل شىء يسألون عنه من الآيات

sources.gloss: He does not send the messengers as lords able to produce every sign they are asked for.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وانما امره بأن يقول ذلك لئلا يدعوا فيه ما أدعت النصارى في المسيح

sources.gloss: He was commanded to say this so that people would not claim about him what the Christians claimed about the Messiah.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني: فلما تركوا ولاية علي أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام وقد أمروا به

sources.gloss: Meaning: when they abandoned the wilaya of Ali, Commander of the Faithful, though they had been commanded to it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ومن أحب بقاء الظالمين فقد أحب أن يعصي الله

sources.gloss: And whoever loves the survival of the wrongdoers has loved that God be disobeyed.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: إنهم لا يصيبهم إلا الجهد والضرر في الدنيا، فأما العذاب الأليم الذي فيه الهلاك فلا يصيب إلا القوم الظالمين

sources.gloss: Nothing but hardship and harm in this world befalls them; as for the painful, destroying punishment, it befalls none but the wrongdoing people.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن أخذ الله منكم الهدى

sources.gloss: If God took the guidance away from you.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: إذا رأيت الله تعالى يعطى على العاصي فانّ ذلك استدراج منه

sources.gloss: If you see God bestowing upon the sinner, that is a gradual enticement from Him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: يا موسى إنّما خزائني إذا أردت شيئاً أن أقول له كن فيكون

sources.gloss: O Musa, My treasuries are only that when I will a thing, I say to it 'Be,' and it is.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وذلك يدل على مذهبنا من أن الله تعالى إذا لم يهده لم يهتد

sources.gloss: That indicates our school's position: if God does not guide a person, he is not guided.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وذلك يدل على أن الهدى والضلال لا يحصلان إلا بهداية الله وإلا بإضلاله

sources.gloss: That shows that guidance and misguidance come about only by God's guiding and by His leading astray.

title.en: Do not drive away the poor

essay.en: These verses close a stretch of arguments set before the polytheists over divine unity and the sign of prophethood, as Tabatabai notes [1]. The Prophet is now told to warn by the Quran those who fear being mustered toward their Lord, before whom they will have neither guardian nor intercessor; Tabrisi glosses 'by it' as the Quran itself [2]. It then turns to the Prophet's own circle: the chiefs of Quraysh had passed by while Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and other poor Muslims sat with him, and demanded that he drive them away before they would follow [3]. God forbids it: do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening desiring His face; you are not accountable for them, nor they for you. To send them away would place him among the wrongdoers. The next verse reads the arrangement as a trial - We test them by one another. Qummi explains it as God trying the rich in how they treat the poor, and the poor in their patience over want [13]. Does God not know best who is grateful? The believers are then to be met with peace, and mercy is promised to whoever does evil in ignorance, then repents and reforms. The passage ends by naming its aim: thus God elaborates the signs, so the way of the guilty stands exposed - and Tabrisi adds that once that path is clear, the believers' path is clear with it [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنذر بالقرآن من يرجون الوصول إلى ربهم برغبتهم فيما عنده، فإن القرآن شافع مشفع

text.en: Warn by the Quran those who hope to reach their Lord through their longing for what is with Him, for the Quran is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ما لي و ما للضياطرة، أطرد قوما غدوا أول النهار يطلبون رزق الله، و آخر النهار ذكروا الله، أ فأطردهم فأكون من الظالمين؟!
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata

text.en: While Ali was giving the Friday sermon, al-Ashath ibn Qays complained that the common folk stood between him and Ali. Ali replied: What have I to do with these arrogant ones? Shall I drive away people who seek God's provision at daybreak and remember Him at nightfall, and so become one of the wrongdoers?

note.en: Tusi holds that 'so that they should say' carries a lam of outcome, not of purpose: God did not test them in order that they deny His favour; that denial was only the result [8].
Tabrisi records several views on whom this verse was revealed about; the reading narrated from al-Sadiq is that it concerns the repentant [4].

narrations.speaker: Ibn Abbas
narrations.arabic: { وإذا جاءك الذين يؤمنون بآياتنا فقل سلام عليكم كتب ربكم على نفسه الرحمة } الآية نزلت … في علي … وحمزة … وزيد
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn al-Hakam al-Habari, from Hasan ibn Husayn, from Habban, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas

text.en: Ibn Abbas said that the verse 'when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say peace to you, your Lord has made mercy incumbent upon Himself' was revealed concerning Ali, Hamza, and Zayd.

perspectives.en: Both traditions report the same occasion and agree the Prophet's honour is preserved, but they weigh it differently. Tusi holds that the prohibition does not mean he drove anyone away: he was capable of the act yet would not commit it, and a warning against it is still fitting [7]. Qurtubi, drawing on Muslim, likewise says the Prophet only inclined inwardly and God forbade him before he acted [30]. Razi allows more: the objectors read a lapse here, but at most it was an error of independent judgment, and such error is forgiven [35].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان احتجاجات متنوعة على المشركين في أمر التوحيد وآية النبوة

sources.gloss: An exposition of various arguments made against the polytheists concerning divine unity and the sign of prophethood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { به } أي بالقرآن عن ابن عباس

sources.gloss: 'By it' means by the Quran (reported from Ibn Abbas).

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: مرّ الملأ من قريش على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عنده صهيب وخباب وبلال وعمار وغيرهم من ضعفاء المسلمين فقالوا يا محمد أرضيت بهؤلاء من قومك أفنحن نكون تَبَعاً لهم أهؤلاء الذين منَّ الله عليهم أطردُهم عنك

sources.gloss: The chiefs of Quraysh passed by the Messenger while Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar and other weak Muslims sat with him, and said: Muhammad, are you content with these of your people? Shall we be their followers? Are these the ones God has favoured? Drive them away from you.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: نزلت في التائبين وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

sources.gloss: It is also said the verse was revealed about the repentant, which is what is narrated from Abu Abdillah (al-Sadiq).

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: المعنى وليستبين سبيل المؤمنين وسبيل المجرمين فحذف لأن ذكر إحدى السبيلين يدلُ على الآخر

sources.gloss: The meaning is that both the way of the believers and the way of the guilty become clear; one is dropped because naming one of the two ways points to the other.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وان لم يقدم على القبيح جاز ان ينهى عنه، لانه قادر عليه

sources.gloss: The Prophet, though he did not commit the ugly act, could still be forbidden from it, since he was capable of it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ولكن اللام لام العاقبة

sources.gloss: Rather the lam here is the lam of outcome (consequence), not of purpose.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: اختبرنا الأغنياء بالغناء لننظر كيف مواساتهم للفقراء وكيف يخرجون ما فرض الله عليهم في أموالهم، فاختبرنا الفقراء لننظر كيف صبرهم على الفقر وعما في أيدي الأغنياء

sources.gloss: We tested the rich with wealth to see how they treat the poor and how they pay out what God made obligatory in their wealth, and We tested the poor to see their patience over poverty and over what the rich possess.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنذر بالقرآن من يرجون الوصول إلى ربهم برغبتهم فيما عنده، فإن القرآن شافع مشفع

sources.gloss: Warn by the Quran those who hope to reach their Lord through their longing for what is with Him, for the Quran is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما لي و ما للضياطرة، أطرد قوما غدوا أول النهار يطلبون رزق الله، و آخر النهار ذكروا الله، أ فأطردهم فأكون من الظالمين؟!

sources.gloss: What have I to do with these arrogant ones? Shall I drive away a people who go out at daybreak seeking God's provision and remember God at nightfall - shall I drive them away and so become one of the wrongdoers?

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: الآية نزلت [ر: قال: نزلت الآية] في علي [بن أبي طالب. ر] وحمزة [وجعفر. ح، ش] وزيد

sources.gloss: This verse was revealed concerning Ali, Hamza, and Zayd.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فنهاه عما همَّ به من الطّرد لا أنه أوقع الطرد

sources.gloss: So God forbade him from the driving away that he had intended, not that he actually carried it out.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فأقصى ما يقال إن هذا الاجتهاد وقع خطأ إلا أن الخطأ في الاجتهاد مغفور

sources.gloss: The utmost that can be said is that this exercise of judgment fell into error, but error in independent judgment is forgiven.

title.en: Judgement and knowledge belong to God

essay.en: The passage is a chain of commands to 'Say,' the Prophet's public answer to those who call on gods beside God. He first disavows their idols: he has been forbidden to worship them, and he will not follow the desires of those who do, for that would leave him astray, outside the ranks of the guided [2]. Tusi records that the Prophet recited this verse at the Ka'ba and openly declared his break with them [5]. He then states his ground: he stands on a manifest proof from his Lord, the Qur'an, which they have denied [1]. The punishment they keep demanding he hasten is not in his hands; judgement belongs to God alone, who parts the truth from the false and is the best of judges [3]. Were it in his hands, the matter between them would be settled at once - but God, who knows the wrongdoers, delays for a wise purpose [7]. The passage then turns from the Prophet's powerlessness to God's boundless reach. With Him are the treasures of the Unseen, which none knows but He [4]; not a leaf falls, nor a grain lies in the earth's darkness, without His knowledge, all held in a manifest Book. Finally He takes the soul in sleep by night, knows the deeds of the day, and wakes it again until the appointed term - death - runs out, when all return to Him for the reckoning [9].

note.en: Reciters differ: 'yaqussu al-haqq,' He recounts the truth, or 'yaqdi al-haqq,' He decides it; Tusi records both readings from the early authorities [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: قال الله عز و جل لمحمد (صلى الله عليه و آله): { قُل لَّوْ أَنَّ عِندِي مَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ لَقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ } قال: لو أني أمرت أن أعلمكم الذي أخفيتم في صدوركم من استعجالكم بموتي لتظلموا أهل بيتي من بعدي
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Hammad, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God said to Muhammad: 'Say, if what you seek to hasten were with me, the matter would be decided between us.' He said: had I been commanded to make known to you what you conceal in your breasts - your haste for my death, that you might wrong my household after me...

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عن قول الله عز و جل: { وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلاَّ يَعْلَمُهَا وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ رَطْبٍ وَلاَ يَابِسٍ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَٰبٍ مُّبِينٍ }. قال: فقال: الورقة: السقط، و الحبة: الولد، و ظلمات الأرض: الأرحام، و الرطب: ما يحيا [من] الناس، و اليابس: ما يغيض، و كل ذلك في إمام مبين
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zayd ibn al-Walid al-Khathami, from Abi al-Rabi al-Shami

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about 'no leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the earth's darkness, nor anything fresh or withered but in a manifest Book.' He said: the leaf is the miscarriage, the grain the child, the earth's darkness the wombs, the fresh what lives, the withered what is discharged - all in a manifest Imam.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { ليقضي أجل مسمى } قال هو الموت
narrations.chain: In the report of Abi al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: In the report of Abi al-Jarud from Abu Jafar, concerning 'so that a specified term may be completed,' he said: it is death.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك و تعالى جعل لملك الموت أعوانا من الملائكة، يقبضون الأرواح بمنزلة صاحب الشرطة له أعوان من الإنس، يبعثهم في حوائجه، فتتوفاهم الملائكة، و يتوفاهم ملك الموت من الملائكة مع ما يقبضه هو، و يتوفاهم الله عز و جل من ملك الموت

text.en: God has given the angel of death helpers from among the angels who seize the souls, as the chief of police has human helpers whom he sends on his errands. The angels take them, the angel of death takes them from the angels, and God takes them from the angel of death.

perspectives.en: Both Shia and Sunni commentators gloss 'the keys of the Unseen' as five matters known to God alone [8][29]. They part over who may share such knowledge. Tusi holds that God opens the door of this knowledge to His chosen prophets and servants, and the Shia narrations read the 'manifest Book' of the falling leaf as the manifest Imam [8][15]. Qurtubi, citing Aisha, holds that whoever claims the Prophet knew what tomorrow holds has invented a grave lie against God, while Tabari reads that 'manifest Book' as the Preserved Tablet [29][22].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فمن هنا يظهر أن الضمير المجرور في قوله { وكذبتم به } راجع إلى البينة لكون المراد به القرآن

sources.gloss: From here it is clear that the pronoun in 'and you have denied it' refers to the manifest proof, since what is meant by it is the Qur'an.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثم أمر الله سبحانه نبيَّه بأن يظهر البراءة مما يعبدونه … { لا أتبع أهواءكم } في عبادتها

sources.gloss: Then God commanded His Prophet to declare his disavowal of what they worship … 'I do not follow your desires' in worshipping them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { يقص الحق } أي يفصل الحق من الباطل

sources.gloss: 'He expounds the truth' means He distinguishes the truth from the false.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وعنده خزائن الغيب … لا يعلمها أحد إلا هو

sources.gloss: With Him are the treasures of the Unseen … none knows them but He.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وروى ابو العالية أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قرأ هذه الآية عند الكعبة وأظهر لهم المفارقة

sources.gloss: Abu al-Aliya reported that the Prophet recited this verse at the Ka'ba and openly showed them his separation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قرأ اهل الحجاز وعاصم { يقص الحق } من القصص … الباقون - بالضاد - المعجمة من فوقها من القضاء

sources.gloss: The people of the Hijaz and Asim read 'yaqussu al-haqq,' from recounting … the rest read it with a pointed dad, from deciding.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والله أعلم بالظالمين } وبمن ينبغي امهاله منهم ومن يجب معالجته بالعقوبة فهو يدبر ذلك بحسب ما يعلم من وجه الحكمة والصواب

sources.gloss: 'And Allah knows best the wrongdoers' - and who among them should be given respite and who should be met with punishment; He orders that according to what wisdom and rightness require.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وروي عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: مفاتح الغيب خمس لا يعلمها الا الله … وأنه الذي يفتح باب العلم لمن يريد إِعلامه شيئا من ذلك من أنبيائه وعباده

sources.gloss: It is reported from Ibn Umar that the Messenger said: the keys of the Unseen are five, none knows them but God … and He is the one who opens the door of that knowledge to whom He wills to inform, of His prophets and servants.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ينيمكم بالليل فيقبضكم الله اليه … { ليقضى أجل مسمى } ليستوفى الاجل المسمى للحياة الى حين الموت. ثم { إليه مرجعكم } يعني يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: He puts you to sleep by night and God takes you to Himself … 'so that a specified term may be completed' - to complete the appointed term of life until death; 'then to Him will be your return' means the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { ليقضي أجل مسمى } قال هو الموت

sources.gloss: In the report of Abi al-Jarud from Abu Jafar concerning 'so that a specified term may be completed': it is death.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لو أني أمرت أن أعلمكم الذي أخفيتم في صدوركم من استعجالكم بموتي لتظلموا أهل بيتي من بعدي

sources.gloss: Had I been commanded to make known to you what you conceal in your breasts - your haste for my death, so that you might wrong my Ahl al-Bayt after me.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الورقة: السقط، و الحبة: الولد، و ظلمات الأرض: الأرحام، و الرطب: ما يحيا [من] الناس، و اليابس: ما يغيض، و كل ذلك في إمام مبين

sources.gloss: The leaf is the miscarriage, the grain the child, the darkness of the earth the wombs, the fresh what lives among people, the withered what is discharged, and all of that is in a manifest Imam.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله تبارك و تعالى جعل لملك الموت أعوانا من الملائكة، يقبضون الأرواح بمنزلة صاحب الشرطة له أعوان من الإنس

sources.gloss: God has given the angel of death helpers from the angels who seize souls, just as the chief of police has human helpers.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: ولا شيء أيضاً مما هو موجود أو مما سيوجد ولم يوجد بعد، إلا وهو مثبت في اللوح المحفوظ

sources.gloss: Nor anything existing, nor anything that will exist and does not yet, but it is fixed in the Preserved Tablet.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: من زعم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخبر بما يكون في غدٍ فقد أعظم على الله الفِرْية

sources.gloss: Whoever claims that the Messenger of God tells what will happen tomorrow has invented a grave lie against God.

essay.en:
These verses carry on the sura's sustained argument against the idolaters, drawing God's oneness, prophethood and the return into one connected sweep [1]. It opens by naming God the All-dominant over His servants, a dominance of power and command, not of place, since being above in location belongs only to bodies [2]. He sends guards who record every deed and will testify on the Day of Rising, and when death arrives His messengers, the helpers of the Angel of Death, take the soul and never fall short [2]. Then all are returned to Allah their true master, to whom alone the judgement belongs, the swiftest of reckoners.

The Prophet is next told to ask who delivers them from the darkness of land and sea, its terrors and hardships, when they call God in humble entreaty and in secret, vowing to be grateful [3]. The answer is given him: it is Allah who saves them from this and from every agony, yet still they ascribe partners to Him [3]. He is equally able to loose a punishment from above them or beneath their feet, or to mix them into warring factions and make them taste one another's violence [4]. The Imams read this threat two ways: as literal ruin like the smoke, the Cry and the swallowing of the earth [16], or as tyrant rulers, evil underlings, partisanship, and mutual bloodshed within the community itself [22].

Though his people deny the truth, the Prophet is no keeper over them [5]; every tiding has its appointed hour, and soon they will know [5]. When he sees men plunging mockingly into God's signs he must withdraw until they turn to other talk, and not sit with wrongdoers once he remembers [6]. The God-wary carry none of the mockers' reckoning but are to remind them, a ruling revealed, al-Tabrisi records, when Muslims feared they could no longer enter the Sacred Mosque [6]. Finally he is to leave those who make their religion a game, warning by the Qur'an lest a soul be handed to ruin, with no guardian, no intercessor, and no ransom accepted [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك و تعالى جعل لملك الموت أعوانا من الملائكة، يقبضون الأرواح بمنزلة صاحب الشرطة له أعوان من الإنس، يبعثهم في حوائجه، فتتوفاهم الملائكة، و يتوفاهم ملك الموت من الملائكة مع ما يقبضه هو، و يتوفاهم الله عز و جل من ملك الموت

text.en: God, Blessed and Exalted, gave the Angel of Death helpers from among the angels, who take the souls as a chief of police has men-helpers he sends on his errands. The angels take them, the Angel of Death takes them from the angels along with what he takes himself, and God takes them from the Angel of Death.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: دخل مروان بن الحكم المدينة … رُدُّوۤاْ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ مَوْلاَهُمُ ٱلْحَقِّ أَلاَ لَهُ ٱلْحُكْمُ وَهُوَ أَسْرَعُ ٱلْحَاسِبِينَ … فقال الحسين (عليه السلام): نعم و الله، رددت أنا و أصحابي إلى الجنة، و رد هو و أصحابه إلى النار
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq

text.en: Marwan ibn al-Hakam entered Medina and reclined, reciting, 'They are returned to Allah, their real master.' al-Husayn said: Yes, by God, I and my companions are returned to Paradise, and he and his companions are returned to the Fire.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ } السلاطين الظلمة، و مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ العبيد السوء و من لا خير فيه … أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً } يعني يضرب بعضكم ببعض بما يلقيه من العداوة و العصبية … وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ } قال: سوء الجوار

text.en: 'From above you' are the tyrant rulers; 'from under your feet' are the evil slaves and those with no good in them; 'or confound you as factions' means He sets you striking one another through the enmity and partisanship He casts between you; 'and make you taste one another's violence' is bad neighbourliness.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وهو القادر على أن يبعث عليكم عذاباً من فوقكم } هو الدخان والصيحة { أو من تحت أرجلكم } وهو الخسف { أو يلبسكم شيعاً } وهو اختلاف في الدين وطعن بعضكم على بعض { ويذيق بعضكم بأس بعض } وهو أن يقتل بعضكم بعضاً. وكل هذا في أهل القبلة
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir

text.en: 'A punishment from above you' is the smoke and the Cry; 'from under your feet' is the swallowing; 'or confound you as factions' is division in religion and mutual attack; 'and make you taste one another's violence' is that you kill one another - and all this is among the people of the qibla.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فلا يجلس في مجلس يسب فيه إمام أو يغتاب فيه مسلم إن الله يقول في كتابه: { فإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا.. }
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudala ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan

text.en: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not sit in a gathering in which an Imam is reviled or a Muslim is backbitten. Indeed God says in His Book: 'When you see those who gossip impiously about Our signs...'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ثَلاثَةُ مَجَالِسَ يَمْقُتُهَا الله وَيُرْسِلُ نَقِمَتَهُ عَلَى أَهْلِهَا فَلا تُقَاعِدُوهُمْ وَلا تُجَالِسُوهُمْ مَجْلِساً فِيهِ مَنْ يَصِفُ لِسَانُهُ كَذِباً فِي فُتْيَاهُ وَمَجْلِساً ذِكْرُ أَعْدَائِنَا فِيهِ جَدِيدٌ وَذِكْرُنَا فِيهِ رَثٌّ وَمَجْلِساً فِيهِ مَنْ يَصُدُّ عَنَّا وَأَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Ishaq ibn Musa, from his brother and uncle, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: There are three gatherings God detests and sends His wrath upon their people; do not sit with them: one where a tongue frames a lie in its ruling, one where our enemies are freshly praised and mention of us worn thin, and one where someone turns people away from us, and you know it.

perspectives.en: Both traditions read 6:68 the same way at its core: the believer must withdraw from any gathering where God's signs are mocked, and must not return once he remembers. They part over how far the verse reaches. The Shia narrations extend it to any assembly where an Imam is reviled or a Muslim is backbitten [17]. The Sunni commentaries widen it to every denier and scoffer: al-Qurtubi cites the ruling that whoever plunges into God's signs is to be shunned, believer or unbeliever [42].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات من تتمة الاحتجاجات على المشركين في التوحيد وما يرتبط به من المعارف في النبوة والمعاد، وهى ذات سياق متصل متسق

sources.gloss: The verses continue the arguments against the polytheists on divine oneness, and the teachings bound up with it in prophethood and the return; they form one connected, coherent context.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لا بمعنى أنه في مكان مرتفع فوقهم وفوق مكانهم لأن ذلك من صفة الأجسام

sources.gloss: Not in the sense that He is in a raised place above them and above their location, for that belongs to the attributes of bodies.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: من ظلمات البر والبحر أي من شدائدهما وأهوالهما

sources.gloss: 'From the darkness of land and sea' means from their hardships and terrors.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي يخلطكم فرقاً مختلفي الأهواء لا تكونون شيعة واحدة

sources.gloss: 'Or confound you as factions' means He mixes you into groups of differing desires, no longer one united body.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لكل خبر من أخبار الله ورسوله حقيقة كائنة إما في الدنيا وإما في الآخرة

sources.gloss: For every tiding of God and His Messenger there is a reality that will come to be, whether in this world or the next.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال المسلمون كيف نصنع إن كان كلما استهزأ المشركون بالقرآن قمنا وتركناهم فلا ندخل إذاً المسجد الحرام

sources.gloss: The Muslims said: how are we to act, if every time the polytheists mock the Qur'an we rise and leave them, so that we can no longer enter the Sacred Mosque?

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي لكي لا تسلم نفس للهلكة بما كسبت

sources.gloss: 'Lest a soul be handed over' means so that no soul is delivered to destruction by what it has earned.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أو يلبسكم شيعاً } وهو اختلاف في الدين وطعن بعضكم على بعض

sources.gloss: 'Or confound you as factions' is division in religion and one of you attacking another.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: من كان يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر فلا يجلس في مجلس يسب فيه إمام أو يغتاب فيه مسلم

sources.gloss: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not sit in a gathering where an Imam is reviled or a Muslim is backbitten.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: جعل لملك الموت أعوانا من الملائكة، يقبضون الأرواح بمنزلة صاحب الشرطة له أعوان من الإنس

sources.gloss: He made for the Angel of Death helpers from among the angels who take the souls, like a chief of police who has men-helpers.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نعم و الله، رددت أنا و أصحابي إلى الجنة، و رد هو و أصحابه إلى النار
