sources.gloss: Yes, by God, I and my companions are returned to Paradise, and he and his companions are returned to the Fire.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: السلاطين الظلمة، و مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ العبيد السوء و من لا خير فيه

sources.gloss: 'From above you' are the tyrant rulers, and 'from under your feet' are the evil slaves and those with no good in them.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: ثَلاثَةُ مَجَالِسَ يَمْقُتُهَا الله وَيُرْسِلُ نَقِمَتَهُ عَلَى أَهْلِهَا فَلا تُقَاعِدُوهُمْ وَلا تُجَالِسُوهُمْ

sources.gloss: There are three gatherings God detests and sends His wrath upon their people; do not sit with them.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: من خاض في آيات الله تُركت مجالسته وهُجر، مؤمناً كان أو كافراً

sources.gloss: Whoever plunges into God's signs, his company is abandoned and he is shunned, whether he is a believer or an unbeliever.

essay.en:
The sura has been teaching the Prophet to answer the idolaters argument by argument, and these verses carry that sequence forward into oneness, prophethood and the return [1]. He is told to ask whether they should call, besides Allah, on what can neither benefit nor harm them, and turn back on their heels after being guided - like a man whom devils have lured into the wilderness, bewildered, stumbling and finding no way, while companions on the road call him to guidance [3]. The answer is fixed: Allah's guidance is the guidance, and the command is to submit, to keep the prayer, and to be wary of the One to whom all are gathered. He created the heavens and the earth in truth, which the commentators read either as created for a true end, not in vain, or as created by His word 'Be' [11], and His is the sovereignty on the day the Trumpet is blown.

The passage then turns to Abraham as the complete example of standing on the religion of the primordial nature and rising for pure oneness [2]. He confronts Azar over the idols; Shia commentators hold that Azar was his grandfather or his uncle, since the Prophet's forefathers back to Adam were believers, not an idol-serving father [12]. Shown the dominion of the heavens and the earth, Abraham watches a star, then the moon, then the sun rise and set, and by each setting he reasons that what disappears cannot be a god but is originated and created [6]. He turns his face to the Originator as a Hanif. When his people dispute with him he refuses to fear their powerless partners and asks which of the two parties better deserves security - which the commentators take as proof that reasoning and argument are required, not blind imitation [16]. The passage closes on its criterion: those who do not taint their faith with wrongdoing, that is with polytheism, have security and are guided [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال: الغيب: ما لم يكن، و الشهادة: ما قد كان.
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The unseen is what has not yet come to be, and the witnessed is what has already come to be.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كشط له عن الأرض ومن عليها وعن السماء ومن فيها والملك الذي يحملها والعرش ومن عليه، وفعل ذلك برسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Darrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: For him the earth was laid bare with all upon it, and the heaven with all within it, and the angel that bears it, and the Throne with all upon it; and the like was done for the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) وقع إلى ثلاثة أصناف: صنف يعبد الزهرة، و صنف يعبد القمر، و صنف يعبد الشمس … فلما جن عليه الليل فرأى الزهرة قال: هذا ربي؟! على الإنكار و الاستخبار، فلما أفل الكوكب قال: لا أحب الآفلين لأن الأفول من صفات المحدث لا من صفات القديم.
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Tamim ibn Abdillah al-Qurashi, from his father, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm

text.en: Abraham came upon three groups: one worshipping Venus, one the moon, one the sun. When night fell and he saw Venus he said, This is my Lord? - in denial and inquiry. When the star set he said, I do not love those that set, for setting is a mark of the originated, not the Eternal.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وسئل أبو عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول إبراهيم هذا ربي أشرك في قوله هذا ربي؟ فقال لا من قال هذا اليوم فهو مشرك، ولم يكن من إبراهيم شرك وإنما كان في طلب ربه وهو من غيره شرك.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Abu Abdillah was asked whether Abraham associated a partner with Allah by saying This is my Lord. He said: No. Whoever says this today is a polytheist, but there was no polytheism from Abraham; he was only seeking his Lord, though from anyone else it would be polytheism.

note.en: Most exegetes read this 'wrongdoing' as polytheism, hearing behind it the word to Luqman's son that polytheism is a grave wrong [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في قوله تعالى: { الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } ، قال: هو الشرك.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Abu Amr al-Zubayri, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning His words, those who have faith and do not taint their faith with wrongdoing, he said: It is polytheism.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عن قول الله عز و جل: { الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } ، قال: بشك.
narrations.chain: al-Kulayni, by his chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Basir

text.en: Abu Basir said: I asked Abu Abdillah about the words those who have faith and do not taint their faith with wrongdoing. He said: With doubt.

perspectives.en: The passage's heart is Abraham's threefold 'This is my Lord' over the star, the moon and the sun. The Shia reading, given by Imam al-Rida before al-Ma'mun, is that he spoke each time in denial and inquiry, never in belief, for a prophet is protected from error and had already known his Lord [25]. Among Sunnis al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Abbas that Abraham worshipped each body until it set, taking the words as a real stage of seeking [38]; but al-Razi records that most verifying scholars reject the idea that a prophet ever said it in genuine belief [61].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات من تتمة الاحتجاجات على المشركين في التوحيد وما يرتبط به من المعارف في النبوة والمعاد، وهى ذات سياق متصل متسق.

sources.gloss: An exposition: these verses complete the arguments against the polytheists concerning divine oneness and the related teachings of prophethood and the return, forming one connected sequence.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والآيات في الحقيقة بيان لمصداق كامل من القيام بدين الفطرة والانتهاض لنشر عقيدة التوحيد والتنزيه عن شرك الوثنية.

sources.gloss: In truth these verses set out a complete example of upholding the religion of the primordial nature and rising to spread the creed of oneness and freedom from idolatrous polytheism.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لأنه قد تحيَّر لاستيلاء الشيطان عليه يهوى ولا يهتدي.

sources.gloss: For he has become bewildered through Satan's mastery over him: he stumbles and finds no guidance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فلما أفل علم أن الأفول لا يجوز على الإله فاستدلَّ بذلك على أنه محدث مخلوق.

sources.gloss: When it set, he knew that setting cannot befit a god, so by it he inferred that the body was originated and created.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والظلم هو الشرك عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب وقتادة ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين.

sources.gloss: The 'wrongdoing' is polytheism, according to Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Qatada, Mujahid and most exegetes.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن والبلخي والجبائي والزجاج والطبري: ان معناه خلقهما للحق لا للباطل … معنى ذلك أنه خلق السماوات والارض بكلامه.

sources.gloss: On 'in truth': al-Hasan, al-Balkhi, al-Jubba'i, al-Zajjaj and al-Tabari say He created them for the truth, not in vain; others say He created the heavens and the earth by His word.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ان آزر كان جده لامه أو كان عمه، لان أباه كان مؤمنا من حيث ثبت عندهم أن آباء النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) الى آدم كلهم كانوا موحدين لم يكن فيهم كافر.

sources.gloss: Azar was his maternal grandfather or his uncle, for his father was a believer, since it is established among them that the Prophet's forefathers up to Adam were all monotheists, with no disbeliever among them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على فساد قول من يقول بالتقليد وتحريم النظر والحجاج، لان الله تعالى مدح ابراهيم لمحاجته لقومه وامر نبيه بالاقتداء به في ذلك.

sources.gloss: The verse shows the falsity of the view that upholds blind imitation and forbids reasoning and argument, for God praised Abraham for arguing with his people and commanded His Prophet to follow him in that.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: كشط له عن الأرض ومن عليها وعن السماء ومن فيها والملك الذي يحملها والعرش ومن عليه.

sources.gloss: For him the earth and all upon it were laid bare, and the heaven and all within it, and the angel that bears it, and the Throne and all upon it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ولم يكن من إبراهيم شرك وإنما كان في طلب ربه وهو من غيره شرك.

sources.gloss: There was no polytheism from Abraham; he was only seeking his Lord, though from anyone else it would be polytheism.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الغيب: ما لم يكن، و الشهادة: ما قد كان.

sources.gloss: The unseen is what has not yet come to be, and the witnessed is what has already come to be.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال: هذا ربي؟! على الإنكار و الاستخبار.

sources.gloss: He said, 'This is my Lord?' - in denial and inquiry, not in affirmation.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال: بشك … قال: هو الشرك.

sources.gloss: Asked about the untainted faith, the Imam glossed the 'wrongdoing' once as doubt (shakk) and once as polytheism (shirk).

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: { فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأى كَوْكَباً قالَ هَذَا رَبي } فعبده حتى غاب، فلما غاب قال: لا أحبّ الآفلين.

sources.gloss: 'When night darkened over him, he saw a star and said, This is my Lord' - and he worshipped it until it disappeared; when it set he said, I do not love those that set (Ibn Abbas, via al-Tabari).

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: واتفق أكثر المحققين على فساد القول الأول واحتجوا عليه بوجوه.

sources.gloss: Most verifying scholars agreed on the falsity of the first view - that Abraham said it in genuine belief - and argued against it on several grounds.

title.en: Abraham and the chain of guidance

essay.en:
Verse 83 closes the long argument Abraham has pressed through this sura: 'This was Our argument that We gave to Abraham against his people.' Al-Tusi draws a rule from it: because God praises this reasoning, disputation and debate in religion are sound, and whoever forbids them has rejected the plain Qur'an [5].

'We raise in rank whomever We wish.' The verses then name the ranks raised: Isaac and Jacob given to Abraham, Noah guided before him, and from the offspring David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, Jesus, Ilyas, Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah and Lot. Tabatabai reads the list not as mere favour but as proof that monotheism is kept among people in an unbroken chain, each link joined to the next by God's guidance [2]. Al-Tusi allows that 'his offspring' may point back to Noah, since all the prophets named descend from him [6]. Jesus is counted among them though he descends only through his mother, Maryam.

Verse 88 turns the roll-call into a warning: 'That is Allah's guidance,' which al-Tabrisi glosses as guidance to reward rather than the mere setting-up of proofs [4]; yet were they to ascribe any partners, what they used to do would not avail them - even these prophets, as al-Qummi notes [8]. Verse 89 grants them the Book, judgement and prophethood, and warns that if 'these' reject them, God has entrusted them to a people who never will. The passage ends by turning to the Prophet: 'So follow their guidance,' and 'I do not ask you any recompense for it,' which al-Qummi reads as no wage sought for the prophethood or the Qur'an [10]. 'It is just an admonition for all the nations.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يا أبا الجارود، ما يقولون لكم في الحسن و الحسين (عليهما السلام)؟ … لأعطينكها من كتاب الله عز و جل أنهما من صلب رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) لا يردها إلا كافر
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Zarif, from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: O Abu al-Jarud, what do they say to you about al-Hasan and al-Husayn? ... I will give you from the Book of God proof that the two are from the loins of the Messenger of God, a proof none rejects but a disbeliever.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هديناهم لنجعل الوصيّة في أهل بيتهم

text.en: We guided them so as to place the succession within their household.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: والله لقد نسب الله عيسى بن مريم في القرآن إلى ابراهيم عليه السّلام من قبل النّساءِ

text.en: By God, God has traced Isa son of Maryam in the Qur'an to Abraham through the side of the women.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: انما اُلْحِقَ عيسى عليه السلام بذراري الأنبياءِ من طريق مريم وكذلك الحقنا بذراري النّبي صلىّ الله عليه وآله وسلم من قبل أمّنا فاطمة عليها السلام

text.en: Isa was joined to the offspring of the prophets through Maryam, and in the same way we were joined to the offspring of the Prophet through our mother Fatimah.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قوماً يقيمون الصلوة ويؤتون الزّكاة ويذكرون الله كثيراً

text.en: A people who establish the prayer, give the alms, and remember God much.

perspectives.en: Verse 89 says that if 'these' disbelieve, God has entrusted the Book, judgement and prophethood to 'a people who will never disbelieve.' Al-Qummi reads 'these' as Quraysh and those who rejected Ali's succession, and the faithful people as the Shia of Ali [9]. The Sunni commentators look elsewhere: al-Tabari relays that the disbelievers are the people of Mecca and the entrusted people the Ansar of Medina [20], while al-Qurtubi records both that they are the Ansar of Medina and the Muhajirun of Mecca and, on Qatada's reading, the prophets just recounted [28].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفي سياق الآيات مضافاً إلى بيان التوحيد بيان أن عقيدة التوحيد محفوظة بين الناس في سلسلة متصلة ركبت حلقاتها بعضها على بعض بهداية إلهية وعناية خاصة ربانية

sources.gloss: In the flow of the verses, besides affirming God's oneness, there is a declaration that the creed of monotheism is preserved among people in a connected chain whose links are set one upon another by divine guidance and a special lordly care.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والهداية هنا هي الإرشاد إلى الثواب دون الهداية التي هي نصب الأدلة

sources.gloss: The guidance here is direction to reward, not the guidance that consists in setting up the proofs.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي ذلك دلالة على صحة المحاجة والمناظرة في الدين والدعاء الى توحيد الله والاحتجاج على الكافرين، لانه تعالى مدح ذلك واستصوبه. ومن حرم الحجاج فقد ردَّ - صريح القرآن

sources.gloss: In this is a proof of the soundness of argument and disputation in religion, of calling to God's oneness and reasoning against the disbelievers, because God praised and approved it; and whoever forbids argument has rejected the plain Qur'an.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله { ومن ذريته } الهاء راجعة الى نوح لان الانبياء المذكورين كلهم من ذريته

sources.gloss: It is possible that in His words 'and from his offspring' the pronoun refers to Noah, because the prophets mentioned are all from his offspring.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني: الأنبياء الذين قد تقدم ذكرهم { لحبط عنهم ما كانوا يعملون }

sources.gloss: Meaning the prophets already mentioned; 'what they used to do would be nullified for them.'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني أصحابه وقريش ومن أنكروا بيعة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام { فقد وكلنا بها قوماً ليسوا بها بكافرين } يعني شيعة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

sources.gloss: Meaning his companions, Quraysh, and those who denied the allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful; 'We have entrusted them to a people who will never disbelieve' means the Shia of the Commander of the Faithful.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قل لقومك: { لا أسئلكم عليه أجراً } يعني على النبوة والقرآن أجراً

sources.gloss: Say to your people, 'I do not ask you any recompense for it' - meaning any wage for the prophethood and the Qur'an.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لأعطينكها من كتاب الله عز و جل أنهما من صلب رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) لا يردها إلا كافر

sources.gloss: I will give you from the Book of God proof that the two are from the loins of the Messenger of God, which none rejects but a disbeliever.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: انما اُلْحِقَ عيسى عليه السلام بذراري الأنبياءِ من طريق مريم وكذلك الحقنا بذراري النّبي صلىّ الله عليه وآله وسلم من قبل أمّنا فاطمة عليها السلام

sources.gloss: Isa was joined to the descendants of the prophets through Maryam, and likewise we were joined to the descendants of the Prophet through our mother Fatimah.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: قال: أهل مكة، فقد وكلنا بها أهل المدينة

sources.gloss: He said: the people of Mecca; and We have entrusted it to the people of Medina.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: يريد الأنصار من أهل المدينة والمهاجرين من أهل مكة. وقال قتادة: يعني النبيّين الذين قصّ الله عز وجل

sources.gloss: He means the Ansar of Medina and the Muhajirun of Mecca; and Qatada said: it means the prophets whom God recounted.

essay.en:
The passage weighs a claim against its Maker: they did not honor God as He deserves when they said, 'Allah has not sent down anything to any human.' Al-Mizan reads this denial as a lowering of God's own station, casting Him out of the rank of a Lord who tends His servants and guides them to their good [1]. Who then, the reply runs, sent down the Book Moses brought as light and guidance, which you cut into parchments, showing some and hiding much? Commentators dispute whether the deniers were Jewish rabbis or the idolaters of Mecca; Tusi holds the Meccan reading fits the flow, since they denied that God sends a book down to a human [6].

Verse 92 answers with the Qur'an itself: a blessed Book confirming what came before, sent to warn the Mother of Cities, Mecca, and, Tabrisi adds, all around it [3]. Those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it and guard their prayers - a sign, Tusi notes, that faith is not held in only part of what God enjoined [7].

Then the gravest wrong: to invent a lie against God, to claim a revelation never given, or to boast, 'I will bring the like of what Allah has sent down.' The scene cuts to the liars in the throes of death, angels' hands outstretched, demanding their souls for a humiliating punishment Tusi records Imam al-Baqir glossing as thirst [8]. All at last come to God alone, stripped of what they were given, intercessors gone.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ الله لا يُوصَفُ وَكَيْفَ يُوصَفُ وَقَدْ قَالَ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَما قَدَرُوا الله حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ فَلا يُوصَفُ بِقَدَرٍ إِلا كَانَ أَعْظَمَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi ibn Abdallah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar

text.en: God cannot be described. How can He be described when He has said in His Book, 'They did not regard Allah with the regard due to Him'? He is not described by any measure but that He is greater than that.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كانوا يكتمون ما شاؤا ويبدون ما شاؤا … كانوا يكتبونه في القراطيس ثم يبدون ما شاؤا ويخفون ما شاؤا

text.en: They used to conceal what they wished and disclose what they wished; in another report: they used to write it on parchments, then disclose what they wished and hide what they wished.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لم سمي النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) الامي؟ … نسب إلى مكة، و ذلك من قول الله: { وَلِتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا } و ام القرى: مكة، فقيل أمي لذلك
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Why was the Prophet called al-Ummi? He said: He was ascribed to Mecca - that is from God's saying, 'so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it' - and the Mother of Cities is Mecca; for that he was called Ummi.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وكان إذا قال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله سميع بصير يكتب سميع عليم … فارتد كافراً ورجع إلى مكة وقال لقريش والله ما يدري محمد ما يقول أنا أقول مثل ما يقول فلا ينكر علي ذلك فأنا أنزل مثل ما أنزل الله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the Messenger of God dictated 'All-hearing, All-seeing,' he would write 'All-hearing, All-knowing.' Then he apostatized and returned to Mecca and said to Quraysh: By God, Muhammad does not know what he says; I say the like of what he says, and it is not held against me; so I send down the like of what God sent down.

note.en: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses the alleged partners as their leaders, and 'all links between you have been cut' as the affection that had bound them [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزلت هذه الآية في معاوية وبني أمية وشركائهم وأئمتهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his father, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: This verse was revealed concerning Mu'awiya, the Banu Umayya, their partners, and their leaders.

perspectives.en: Sunni and Shia agree that to deny revelation is to fail God's due. But they take 'they did not regard Allah with the regard due to Him' in different directions. Al-Qurtubi and al-Razi read it within its setting: the deniers did not magnify God, nor know Him as He deserves, when they rejected His messengers [24][28]. The Shia narrations lift the phrase into pure transcendence. Imam al-Hadi joins it to the verse where the whole earth is God's handful on the Day of Resurrection, reading both as one failure - God's rebuke of everyone who likens Him to His creation [44].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فإن في إنكار إنزال الوحي حطاً لقدره تعالى وإخراجاً له من منزلة الربوبية المعتنية بشؤون عباده وهدايتهم إلى هدفهم من السعادة والفلاح.

sources.gloss: For in denying the sending down of revelation there is a lowering of His station and a removal of Him from the rank of a Lord who attends to His servants' affairs and their guidance to their goal of happiness and success.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعني بأم القرى مكة ومن حولها أهل الأرض كلهم عن ابن عباس.

sources.gloss: By 'the Mother of Cities' is meant Mecca, and 'those around it' is all the people of the earth, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال مجاهد نزلت في مشركي قريش، وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس أيضا، وهو أشبه بسياق الآية، لانهم الذين أنكروا أن يكون الله أنزل كتابا على بشر، دون اليهود والنصارى.

sources.gloss: Mujahid said it was revealed about the idolaters of Quraysh - reported also from Ibn Abbas - and that is closer to the flow of the verse, for they are the ones who denied that God sent down a book to a human, unlike the Jews and Christians.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهذا يقوي مذهبنا في انه لا يجوز ان يكون مؤمنا ببعض ما أوجب الله عليه دون بعض.

sources.gloss: This strengthens our position that one may not be a believer in part of what God has enjoined upon him but not the rest.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وعن ابي جعفر (ع) عذاب الهون يعني العطش.

sources.gloss: From Abu Jafar: the humiliating punishment means thirst.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فارتد كافراً ورجع إلى مكة وقال لقريش والله ما يدري محمد ما يقول أنا أقول مثل ما يقول فلا ينكر علي ذلك فأنا أنزل مثل ما أنزل الله

sources.gloss: He apostatized and returned to Mecca and said to Quraysh: By God, Muhammad does not know what he says; I say the like of what he says, and it is not held against me; so I send down the like of what God sent down.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: والشركاء أئمتهم { لقد تقطع بينكم } يعني: المودة … نزلت هذه الآية في معاوية وبني أمية وشركائهم وأئمتهم

sources.gloss: The partners are their leaders; 'all links between you have been cut' means the affection... This verse was revealed concerning Mu'awiya, the Banu Umayya, their partners, and their leaders.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نسب إلى مكة، و ذلك من قول الله: { وَلِتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا } و ام القرى: مكة، فقيل أمي لذلك

sources.gloss: He was ascribed to Mecca. That is from God's saying, 'so that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it.' The Mother of Cities is Mecca; for that he was called Ummi.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: كانوا يكتمون ما شاؤا ويبدون ما شاؤا … كانوا يكتبونه في القراطيس ثم يبدون ما شاؤا ويخفون ما شاؤا

sources.gloss: They used to conceal what they wished and disclose what they wished; in another report: they used to write it on parchments, then disclose what they wished and hide what they wished.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وقال الحسن: ما عظّموه حقَّ عظمته … وقال أبو عبيدة: أي ما عرفوا الله حقّ معرفته.

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan said: they did not magnify Him as He deserves to be magnified... Abu Ubayda said: they did not know God as He truly should be known.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس: ما عظموا الله حق تعظيمه … وقال الأخفش: ما عرفوه حق معرفته.

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: they did not magnify God with the magnifying due to Him... al-Akhfash said: they did not know Him as He truly should be known.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: إِنَّ الله لا يُوصَفُ وَكَيْفَ يُوصَفُ وَقَدْ قَالَ فِي كِتَابِهِ وَما قَدَرُوا الله حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ فَلا يُوصَفُ بِقَدَرٍ إِلا كَانَ أَعْظَمَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ.

sources.gloss: God cannot be described. How can He be described when He has said in His Book, 'They did not regard Allah with the regard due to Him'? He is not described by any measure but that He is greater than that.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: ذلك تعيير الله تبارك و تعالى لمن شبهه بخلقه … كما قال عز وجل: وما قدروا الله حق قدره إذ قالوا ما أنزل الله على بشر من شئ

sources.gloss: That is God's rebuke of the one who likens Him to His creation... as He said: 'They did not regard Allah with the regard due to Him' when they said, 'Allah has not sent down anything to any human.'

essay.en: After the dispute with those who denied revelation, the sura turns to a run of signs that set out His oneness through His names and works [1]. Grain and pit are split so that crop and tree come forth; the living emerges from the dead and the dead from the living. 'That is Allah! Then where do you stray?' The commentators read 'splitter' (faliq) as the One who cleaves the dry, dead seed so a plant grows, though some early authorities gloss it simply as 'creator' [2][6]. Dawn is cleft from the night's darkness, the night is made a place of rest, and the sun and moon run 'for calculation,' the ordaining of 'the All-mighty, the All-knowing' [7]. He set the stars so travelers may be guided through 'the darkness of land and sea' [8]. He raised all people from a single soul, Adam, and appointed for them an abode and a lodging-place [9]. He sends down water, from the clouds, and brings out every growing thing [4]: green shoots, clustered grain, low-hanging dates, gardens of grapes, olives and pomegranates, 'similar and dissimilar,' and bids the reader watch the fruit ripen. The passage closes by turning on those who make the jinn partners of God, though He created them, and who 'carve out sons and daughters for Him, without any knowledge.' Tabrisi notes that the jinn here are read as the angels, called jinn because they are hidden from sight [5]. Immaculate is He, and exalted above what they allege.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فَالْحَبُّ طِينَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّتِي أَلْقَى الله عَلَيْهَا مَحَبَّتَهُ وَالنَّوَى طِينَةُ الْكَافِرِينَ الَّذِينَ نَأَوْا عَنْ كُلِّ خَيْرٍ … فَالْحَيُّ الْمُؤْمِنُ وَالْمَيِّتُ الْكَافِرُ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When God willed to create Adam, He parted two clays and then mixed them. Hence His word: the grain is the believers' clay, on which He cast His love; the pit is the clay of the unbelievers, who withdrew from all good. The living is the believer; the dead, the unbeliever.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الحب: ما أحبه، و النوى: ما نأى عن الحق فلم يقبله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The grain (al-habb) is what He loves, and the pit (al-nawa) is what withdrew from the truth and would not accept it.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ولا تسر أوّل اللّيل فانّ الله جعله سكناً وقدّره مقاماً لا ظعناً فأرح فيه بدنك

text.en: Do not travel in the first part of the night, for God has made it a rest and appointed it a place to stay, not to journey; so rest your body in it.

note.en: The commentary of Ali ibn Ibrahim reads the stars figuratively: they are the family of Muhammad, by whom the believer is guided through the darkness of land and sea [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: المستقر: ما استقر الإيمان في قلبه فلا ينزع منه أبدا، و المستودع: الذي يستودع الإيمان زمانا ثم يسلبه، و قد كان الزبير منهم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: They lie who say it means settled in the womb and deposited in the loins. The abode is faith fixed in the heart, never removed; the lodging is faith lent for a time then stripped away. Al-Zubayr was one of these.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: خلق النّبيينّ على النبوّة فلا يكونون إلاّ أنبياء وخلق المؤمنين على الإيمان فلا يكونون إلاّ مؤمنين وأعار قوماً إيماناً فان شاء تممه لهم وان شاء سلبهم إيّاه … وفيهم جرت فمستقر ومستودع

text.en: God created the prophets for prophethood, so they can only be prophets, and the believers for faith, so they can only be believers. But a people He lent faith: if He wills He completes it for them, and if He wills He strips them of it. Of these was 'an abode and a lodging' revealed.

perspectives.en: On 'an abode and a lodging-place' (6:98) the two traditions part. The Sunni commentators keep to the body: Tabari and Ibn Kathir report that the abode is the womb and the lodging the loins, or the abode this world and the lodging the place where one dies [25][29]. The Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt add an inward reading: the abode is faith fixed in the heart and never removed, the lodging faith only lent for a time and then stripped away, as with al-Zubayr [18]. One reading traces the body's passage, the other the soul's; on the verse's plain sense both agree.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ثم تتخلص إلى ذكر آيات توحيده تعالى وذكر أشياء من أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا

sources.gloss: Then [the passage] moves on to mention the signs of His oneness and something of His beautiful names and lofty attributes.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي شاق الحبة اليابسة الميتة فيخرج منها النبات وشاق النواة اليابسة فيخرج منها النخل والشجر

sources.gloss: That is, He splits the dry, dead grain so the plant comes forth from it, and splits the dry pit so the palm and tree come forth from it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يريد من السحاب والعرب تقول كلُّ ما علاك فأطلَّك فهو سماء

sources.gloss: He means from the clouds; the Arabs call whatever rises above you and shades you 'sky.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأراد بالجن الملائكة وإنما سمّاهم جِنّاً لاستتارهم عن الأَعين

sources.gloss: By 'the jinn' He meant the angels; He called them jinn only because they are concealed from eyes.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الضحاك وابن عباس: معنى { فالق الحب والنوى } خالقهما

sources.gloss: Dahhak and Ibn Abbas said the meaning of 'splitter of the grain and the pit' is their creator.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى قوله { فالق الإصباح } أي شاق عمود الصبح عن ظلمة الليل

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'splitter of the dawn' is: He cleaves the column of dawn from the darkness of the night.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: جعل لهم النجوم بمعنى خلقها ليهتدوا بها في اسفارهم في ظلمات البر والبحر

sources.gloss: He made for them the stars, meaning He created them, so they may be guided by them in their journeys through the darkness of land and sea.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أنشأ الخلق ابتداء من نفس واحدة يعني آدم، منهم مستقر ومستودع

sources.gloss: He originated creation from a single soul, meaning Adam; among them is one in the abode and one in lodging.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال: النجوم آل محمد عليهم السلام

sources.gloss: He said: the stars are the family of Muhammad, peace be upon them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الحب: ما أحبه، و النوى: ما نأى عن الحق فلم يقبله

sources.gloss: The grain is what He loves, and the pit is what withdrew from the truth and did not accept it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: المستقر: ما استقر الإيمان في قلبه فلا ينزع منه أبدا، و المستودع: الذي يستودع الإيمان زمانا ثم يسلبه

sources.gloss: The abode (mustaqarr) is faith that has settled in the heart and is never removed; the lodging (mustawda) is faith deposited for a time then stripped away.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ولا تسر أوّل اللّيل فانّ الله جعله سكناً وقدّره مقاماً لا ظعناً فأرح فيه بدنك

sources.gloss: Do not travel in the first part of the night, for God has made it a rest and appointed it a place to stay, not to journey; so rest your body in it.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وأعار قوماً إيماناً فان شاء تممه لهم وان شاء سلبهم إيّاه

sources.gloss: And He lent a people faith: if He wills He completes it for them, and if He wills He strips them of it.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: فمنكم مستقرّ في الرحم ومنكم مستودع في القبر

sources.gloss: Of you some are settled in the womb and some deposited in the grave.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فمستقر أي في الأرحام، قالوا، أو أكثرهم ومستودع أي في الأصلاب

sources.gloss: 'An abode' means in the wombs, and - they said, or most of them - 'a lodging' means in the loins.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: فَالْحَبُّ طِينَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّتِي أَلْقَى الله عَلَيْهَا مَحَبَّتَهُ وَالنَّوَى طِينَةُ الْكَافِرِينَ الَّذِينَ نَأَوْا عَنْ كُلِّ خَيْرٍ

sources.gloss: The grain is the clay of the believers, upon which God cast His love; the pit is the clay of the unbelievers, who withdrew from all good.

title.en: There is no god but Him

essay.en:
The passage answers those who assigned God a partner or a child. Tabatabai notes that it turns to display the signs of God's oneness and some of His most beautiful names [1]. He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who brought them into being on no prior model; Tusi holds that this origination belongs to God alone, since no one else creates without a pattern to follow [9]. So how could He have a child when He has no consort, He who created all things?

'That is Allah, your Lord, there is no god except Him, the creator of all things; so worship Him.' The One who holds these attributes is alone worthy of worship, and He watches over all things as their guardian [10]. Then the passage sets Him beyond the reach of sight: 'The sights do not apprehend Him, yet He apprehends the sights.'

'Certainly insights have come to you from your Lord.' These are proofs by which a person tells guidance from error; whoever sees benefits his own soul, and whoever stays blind harms himself, which shows that people act by their own choice and are not compelled [5]. Al-Qummi reads the verse as a refutation of those who deny that man has any act of his own [21].

The signs are turned about in many ways, yet the deniers still claimed the Prophet had only been taught them, saying he learned his reports from the scholars of the Jews [22]. He is told to follow what is revealed of tawhid and not be turned aside by the arrogance of the idolaters [2]; some hold the order to turn away from them was later abrogated by the command to fight [23]. Had God willed, they would not have ascribed partners; the Imams explain that He could have made all people infallible, but instead He tested them and gave them the means to earn reward [6].

The believers are then forbidden to abuse the idols, lest the idolaters abuse God in ignorance [7]. Finally the Quraysh swear that a sign would make them believe, yet God knows they would not [26], and He leaves them bewildered in their rebellion.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إحاطة الوهم … إنما عنى إحاطة الوهم، كما يقال: فلان بصير بالشعر، و فلان بصير بالفقه، و فلان بصير بالدراهم، و فلان بصير بالثياب، الله أعظم من أن يرى بالعين
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is the encompassing of the imagination. He only meant the encompassing of the imagination, as one says a man is discerning in poetry, discerning in jurisprudence, discerning in coins, discerning in cloth. God is too great to be seen by the eye.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إن أوهام القلوب أكبر من أبصار العيون فهو لا تدركه الاوهام وهو يدرك الاوهام
narrations.chain: al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: Truly the imaginings of the heart are greater than the sight of the eyes; He is not reached by the imaginings, and He reaches the imaginings.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان المؤمنون يسبون ما يعبد المشركون من دون الله وكان المشركون يسبون ما يعبد المؤمنون فنهى الله المؤمنين عن سب آلهتم لكيلا يسب الكفار إله المؤمنين فيكونوا المؤمنون قد أشركوا بالله من حيث لا يعلمون
narrations.chain: his father, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The believers used to abuse what the idolaters worship besides God, and the idolaters would abuse what the believers worship. So God forbade the believers from abusing their gods, lest the disbelievers abuse the God of the believers, and the believers thereby fall into idolatry from where they do not know.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا عمر، هل رأيت أحدا يسب الله؟ … من سب ولي الله فقد سب الله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Umar al-Tayalisi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Umar, have you seen anyone abuse God? … Whoever abuses the friend of God has abused God.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ننكس قلوبهم فيكون أسفل قلوبهم أعلاها ونعمي أبصارهم فلا يبصرون بالهدى … كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة يعني: في الذر والميثاق
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: We invert their hearts so that the lowest of their hearts becomes the highest, and We blind their eyes so they do not see by the guidance. 'As they did not believe in it the first time' means in the realm of the atoms and the covenant.

perspectives.en: The commentators divide over whether God can ever be seen. Tabrisi and Tusi read 'the sights do not apprehend Him' as an outright denial: Tusi holds it is a praise God gives Himself, and what He praises by negating would be a defect if affirmed, so vision of Him is impossible; Tabrisi glosses the verse plainly as 'the eyes do not see Him' [11][4]. The Sunni exegetes hold that the verse denies only that eyes encompass Him in this world, while the believers will see their Lord in the hereafter; Ibn Kathir and al-Razi cite 'looking toward their Lord' and read the verse as proof that such vision is possible [45][62].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ثم تتخلص إلى ذكر آيات توحيده تعالى وذكر أشياء من أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا

sources.gloss: Then it passes to mentioning the signs of His oneness and some of His most beautiful names and lofty attributes.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أمر باتباع ما أُوحي إليه من ربه من أمر التوحيد وأُصول شرائع الذين من غير أن يصده ما يشاهده من استكبار المشركين عن الخضوع لكلمة الحق والإِعراض عن دعوة الدين

sources.gloss: A command to follow what his Lord revealed to him of tawhid and the foundations of the religion's laws, without letting the arrogance he witnesses in the idolaters, their refusal to submit to the word of truth and their turning from the call of the faith, hold him back.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { لا تدركه الأَبصار } أي لا تراه العيون

sources.gloss: 'The sights do not apprehend Him' means the eyes do not see Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذا دلالة على أن المكلفين مخيّرون في أفعالهم غير مجبرين

sources.gloss: In this is a proof that the accountable are given a choice in their acts, not compelled.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي تفسير أهل البيت ع لو شاء الله أن يجعلهم كلهم مؤمنين معصومين حتى كان لا يعصيه أحد لما كان يحتاج إلى جنة ولا إلى نار ولكنه أمرهم ونهاهم وامتحنهم

sources.gloss: In the interpretation of the People of the House: had God willed to make them all believers, protected so that none would disobey Him, He would have had no need of a Paradise or a Fire; but He commanded them, forbade them, and tested them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثم نهى الله المؤمنين أن يسبُّوا الأَصنام لما في ذلك من المفسدة

sources.gloss: Then God forbade the believers to abuse the idols, because of the harm in it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واما بديع السماوات والأرض فلا يوصف به غير الله لانه خالقهما على غير مثال سبق

sources.gloss: As for 'the Originator of the heavens and the earth,' none but God is described by it, for He created them on no prior model.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والوكيل على الشيء هو الحافظ الذي يحوطه ويدفع الضرر عنه

sources.gloss: The guardian (wakil) over a thing is the keeper who surrounds it and wards off harm from it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: في هذه الآية دلالة واضحة على انه تعالى لا يرى بالابصار، لانه تمدح بنفي الادراك عن نفسه

sources.gloss: In this verse is a clear proof that He is not seen by the sights, for He praised Himself by denying apprehension of Himself.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهو رد على المجبرة الذين يزعمون أنه ليس لهم فعل ولا اكتساب

sources.gloss: It is a refutation of the predestinarians, who claim that people have no act and no acquisition of their own.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: كانت قريش تقول لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله إن الذي تخبرنا به من الأخبار تتعلمه من علماء اليهود وتدرسه

sources.gloss: The Quraysh used to say to the Messenger of God: what you tell us of these reports you learn from the scholars of the Jews and study.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: منسوخ بقوله اقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم

sources.gloss: Abrogated by His words, 'Kill the idolaters wherever you find them.'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فنهى الله المؤمنين عن سب آلهتم لكيلا يسب الكفار إله المؤمنين فيكونوا المؤمنون قد أشركوا بالله من حيث لا يعلمون

sources.gloss: So God forbade the believers from abusing their gods, lest the disbelievers abuse the God of the believers, and the believers thereby become idolaters from where they do not know.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ثم حكى قولهم وهم قريش

sources.gloss: Then He related their saying, and they are the Quraysh.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ننكس قلوبهم فيكون أسفل قلوبهم أعلاها ونعمي أبصارهم فلا يبصرون بالهدى

sources.gloss: We invert their hearts so the lowest of them becomes the highest, and We blind their eyes so they do not see by the guidance.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الله أعظم من أن يرى بالعين

sources.gloss: God is too great to be seen by the eye.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: من سب ولي الله فقد سب الله

sources.gloss: Whoever abuses the friend of God has abused God.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: لا تدركه في الدنيا، وإن كانت تراه في الآخرة

sources.gloss: Eyes do not apprehend Him in this world, though they will see Him in the hereafter.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: احتج أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أنه تعالى تجوز رؤيته والمؤمنين يرونه يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: Our companions argued from this verse that His being seen is possible, and that the believers will see Him on the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad asif al-muhsini

excerpt.text: إن أوهام القلوب أكبر من أبصار العيون فهو لا تدركه الاوهام وهو يدرك الاوهام

sources.gloss: The imaginings of the heart are greater than the sight of the eyes; imaginings do not reach Him, and He reaches the imaginings.

essay.en:
The passage opens by answering a demand for miracles. Even if angels came down, the dead spoke to them, and everything were gathered before them, the obstinate would still not believe unless God willed it - which al-Tabrisi and al-Tusi read as God compelling them, since such men never believe by free choice [3][10]. Al-Tabrisi notes that this reading is reported from the Ahl al-Bayt [3], and al-Mizan adds that guidance follows the order of causes: whoever turns from God's mercy is left in his error [1].

The sura then consoles the Prophet. For every prophet God appointed enemies, satans among men and jinn who trade flashy speech to deceive, as He did for the messengers before him [4][11]. Toward that speech the hearts of those who deny the Hereafter incline.

The turn comes at verse 114: shall the Prophet seek any judge but God, who has sent down the Book well-elaborated? Al-Tabrisi explains that 'judge' stands above 'ruler,' for it names only one who decides by the truth [5]. God's word is complete in truth and justice, and nothing alters it - truth in its reports, justice in its rulings [6]. To obey most people on earth is to be led astray, for they follow only conjecture; the measure is proof, not numbers, since the truth may lie with the few [7].

The passage closes with food. Eat what God's name is pronounced over; why refuse it, when He has already detailed the forbidden, except under compulsion? Do not eat what His name was not named over, for that is transgression, and the satans prompt their friends to dispute the point. Al-Mizan, following Ibn Abbas, ties this to the idolaters' taunt: you eat what you kill, yet not what God kills [2]. To obey them here is to share in their idolatry.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الشياطين يلقى بعضهم بعضا فيلقي إليه ما يغوي به الخلق حتى يتعلم بعضهم من بعض

text.en: The satans meet one another, and each casts to the other what he leads people astray with, so that they learn it from one another.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما بعث الله نبيا إلا و في أمته شيطانان يؤذيانه و يضلان الناس بعده، فأما صاحبا نوح فقيطفوص و خرام، و أما صاحبا إبراهيم فمكثل و رزام، و أما صاحبا موسى فالسامري و مرعتيبا، و أما صاحبا عيسى فبولس، و مرتيون، و أما صاحبا محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) فحبتر و زريق
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God sent no prophet without two satans in his community who harmed him and misled people after him: for Nuh, Qaytafus and Kharam; for Ibrahim, Makthal and Razam; for Musa, al-Samiri and Mar'atiba; for Isa, Bulus and Martiyun; and for Muhammad, Habtar and Zurayq.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إذا خلق الله الإمام في بطن أمه يكتب على عضده الأيمن … وتمت كلمة ربك صدقاً وعدلاً لا مبدل لكلماته وهو السميع العليم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When God creates the Imam in his mother's womb, He writes on his right arm: 'The word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; nothing can change His words, and He is the All-hearing, the All-knowing.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فإذا ولد بعث الله ذلك الملك إلى الإِمام أن يكتب بين عينيه … فإذا مضى ذلك الإمام الذي قبله رفع له مناراً يبصر به أعمال العباد
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Humayd ibn Shu'ayb, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When the Imam is born, God sends that angel to write between his eyes the same verse; and when the Imam before him passes away, God raises for him a beacon by which he sees the deeds of the servants.

narrations.speaker: Imam Musa ibn Jafar
narrations.arabic: يَا هِشَامُ ثُمَّ ذَمَّ الله الْكَثْرَةَ فَقَالَ وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الارْضِ يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ الله
narrations.chain: Abu Abdillah al-Ash'ari, from some of our companions, raising it, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam

text.en: O Hisham, God then disparaged the multitude, saying: 'If you obey most of those on the earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أنّه سئل عن مجوسّي قال بسم الله وذبح فقال كل فقيل مسلم ذبح ولم يسمّ فقال لا تأكل إنّ الله يقول فكلوا ممّا ذكر اسم الله عليه ولا تأكلوا ممّا لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

text.en: He was asked about a Magian who said 'In the name of God' and slaughtered. He said: Eat. It was said: a Muslim slaughtered but did not name God. He said: Do not eat; God says, 'Eat from that over which God's name has been mentioned.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنّه سئل عن رجل ذبح فسبّح أو كبّر أو هلّل أو حمد الله قال هذا كله من أسماء الله تعالى ولا بأس به

text.en: He was asked about a man who slaughtered and said 'Glory be to God,' or 'God is greater,' or 'There is no god but God,' or praised God. He said: All these are among the names of God, and there is no harm in it.

note.en: Al-Qummi glosses the outward sin as acts of disobedience and the inward as idolatry and doubt in the heart [29].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا تأكل ذبيحته حتى تسمعه يذكر اسم الله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Humran, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning the slaughter of a hostile opponent and a Jew, he said: Do not eat his slaughter until you hear him mention the name of God. Have you not heard God's word, 'Do not eat of that over which God's name has not been mentioned'?

perspectives.en: The traditions divide over naming God at the slaughter. Al-Tabrisi reports the Imams' ruling: if a Muslim omits the name forgetfully the meat stays lawful, provided he holds the naming obligatory, but if he omits it deliberately the meat is unlawful [9]. Sunni jurists are split, as al-Razi records: Malik and Abu Hanifa treat deliberate omission as disqualifying, while al-Shafi'i holds the naming only recommended and confines the prohibition to what is slaughtered for idols, so a qualified slaughterer's meat remains lawful either way [76].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: كذلك السنة في نظام التشريع والهداية هي سنة الأسباب فمن استرحم الله رحمه ومن أعرض عن رحمته حرمه

sources.gloss: So too the way of guidance follows the order of causes: whoever seeks God's mercy, He shows him mercy, and whoever turns from His mercy, He deprives him.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أن المشركين خاصموا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمؤمنين في أمر الميتة قائلين أتاكلون مما قتلتم أنتم ولا تأكلون مما قتله الله

sources.gloss: That the idolaters disputed with the Prophet and the believers about carrion, saying, 'Do you eat what you kill and not what God kills?'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن يجبرهم على الإِيمان عن الحسن وهو المروي عن أهل البيت

sources.gloss: 'Unless God wishes' - that He compel them to believe, on the authority of al-Hasan, and this is what is reported from the Ahl al-Bayt.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثُمَّ بينَّ ما كان عليه حال الأَنبياء ع مع أعدائهم تسلية لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: Then He explained the state of the prophets with their enemies, as a consolation for His Prophet.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: الحكم والحاكم بمعنى واحد إلاَّ إن الحكم أَمدح لأن معناه من يستحق أن يتحاكم إليه فهو لا يقضي إلاَّ بالحق

sources.gloss: 'Judge' (hakam) and 'ruler' (hakim) mean the same, except that hakam is more praiseworthy, for it means one who deserves to be resorted to for judgment and who decides only by the truth.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ما كان في القرآن من الأخبار فهو صدق لا يشوبه كذب وما فيهِ من الأمر والنهي والحكم والإباحة والحظر فهو عدل

sources.gloss: Whatever in the Quran is a report is truth unmixed with falsehood, and whatever is command, prohibition, ruling, permission and interdiction is justice.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لا عبرة في دين الله ومعرفة الحق بالقلة والكثرة لجواز أن يكون الحق مع الأَقلّ وإنما الإعتبار فيه بالحجة دون القلة والكثرة

sources.gloss: In God's religion and the knowledge of truth, fewness and multitude count for nothing, for the truth may be with the fewer; what counts is proof, not fewness or multitude.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يحلُّ أكلها إذا ترك التسمية ناسياً بعد أن يكون معتقداً لوجوبها ويحرم أكلها وإذا تركها متعمداً … وهو المروي عن أئمتنا ع

sources.gloss: Its meat is lawful if the naming was left out forgetfully, provided he believes it obligatory, and unlawful if he left it out deliberately - and this is what is reported from our Imams.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن: إِلا أن يشاء الله أن يجبرهم على الايمان بأن يمنعهم من اضداد الايمان كلها فيقع منهم الايمان

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan said: 'unless God wishes' means that He compel them to believe by barring them from all that opposes faith, so that faith occurs from them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهذا القول من الله تعالى تسلية للنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) في أنه أجراه مجرى غيره من الانبياء

sources.gloss: This word of God is a consolation to the Prophet, in that He treated him as He treated the other prophets.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: إذا خلق الله الإمام في بطن أمه يكتب على عضده الأيمن

sources.gloss: When God creates the Imam in his mother's womb, He writes on his right arm the verse.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: الظاهر من الإِثم المعاصي والباطن الشرك والشك في القلب

sources.gloss: The outward of sin is acts of disobedience, and the inward is idolatry and doubt in the heart.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الشياطين يلقى بعضهم بعضا فيلقي إليه ما يغوي به الخلق حتى يتعلم بعضهم من بعض

sources.gloss: The satans meet one another, and each casts to the other what he leads people astray with, so that they learn from one another.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا تأكل ذبيحته حتى تسمعه يذكر اسم الله

sources.gloss: Do not eat his slaughter until you hear him mention the name of God.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: سئل عن مجوسّي قال بسم الله وذبح فقال كل فقيل مسلم ذبح ولم يسمّ فقال لا تأكل

sources.gloss: He was asked about a Magian who said 'In the name of God' and slaughtered; he said: Eat. It was said: a Muslim slaughtered but did not name God; he said: Do not eat.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وقال الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى: يحل متروك التسمية سواء ترك عمداً أو خطأ إذا كان الذابح أهلاً للذبح

sources.gloss: Al-Shafi'i said: the meat over which the naming was left out is lawful, whether omitted deliberately or by mistake, so long as the slaughterer is qualified to slaughter.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: يَا هِشَامُ ثُمَّ ذَمَّ الله الْكَثْرَةَ فَقَالَ وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الارْضِ يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ الله

sources.gloss: O Hisham, then God disparaged the multitude, saying: 'If you obey most of those on the earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah.'

essay.en:
The passage opens with a parable [3]. A man was lifeless; God gave him life and 'a light by which he walks among the people,' unlike one lost in 'a manifold darkness which he cannot leave.' Tabrisi reads the death as disbelief and the life as faith, and the light as knowledge, the Quran, or faith itself [3]. Tusi adds that the verse makes seeking knowledge an obligation, since God likens it to life for perception and to light for guidance [8]. The occasion was disputed - Umar, or Ammar, against Abu Jahl - but the general reading, of every believer and disbeliever, is preferred as more comprehensive [3]. Beneath the plain image, Tabatabai finds an enduring life that worldly death does not cut off [1].

Then God says He installed 'in every town its major criminals' to plot, though their plotting recoils only on themselves. Tusi notes that the 'that they may plot' is the lam of consequence, not of purpose, for God does not will their scheming [9]. When a sign reached them, they demanded prophethood of their own kind, out of envy, and God answered, 'Allah knows best where to place His apostleship' - apostleship, Tusi explains, follows the people's welfare [10].

Whomever God desires to guide, He opens the breast to Islam; whomever He desires to lead astray, He makes the breast narrow. Tabrisi reads the opening as grace and reward, and the straitening as a punishment for refusing faith, not a barring from it [5]. A report has the Prophet call the opening a light God casts into the heart, its sign a turning toward the abode of eternity [25]. This, the passage says, is 'the straight path of your Lord' - the Quran, or Islam [6] - and for those who heed it, 'the abode of peace near their Lord.'

It closes at the gathering, where the jinn and their human friends are consigned to the Fire. Tabatabai insists that the decree there does not strip their choice, so it is no injustice [2]; and, al-Baqir says, God requites one wrongdoer only by means of another [27].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ميت لا يعرف شيئا { نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ } إماما يأتم به { كَمَن مَّثَلُهُ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِّنْهَا } … الذي لا يعرف الإمام
narrations.chain: al-Kulayni, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Burayd, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The dead man is one who knows nothing. 'A light by which he walks among the people' is an Imam whom he follows. 'Like one in a darkness he cannot leave' is the one who does not know the Imam.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: جاهلاً عن الحق والولاية فهديناه إليها … قال النور الولاية { كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها } يعني: في ولاية غير الأئمة عليهم السلام

text.en: He was ignorant of the truth and the guardianship, so We guided him to it. The light is the guardianship; 'like one in a darkness he cannot leave' means being in the guardianship of other than the Imams.

narrations.speaker: Zayd ibn Ali
narrations.arabic: أيها الناس إن الله بعث في كل زمان خيرة ومن كل خيرة منتجباً … قال: { الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته } فلم يزل يتناسخ خيرته حتى خرج محمد … من أفضل تربة وأطهر عترة أخرجت للناس
narrations.chain: Furat, from Ja'far ibn Ahmad, from Zayd ibn Ali

text.en: O people, God raised up in every age a chosen group, and from every chosen group a select one. 'Allah knows best where He places His message.' His elect kept passing down until Muhammad came forth from the best soil and the purest lineage brought forth for the people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قد يكون ضيّقاً وله منفذ يسمع منه ويبصر والحَرِج هو الملتأم الذي لا منفذ له يسمع به ولا يبصر منه
narrations.chain: in al-Maani, from al-Sadiq

text.en: The narrow breast still has an opening through which he hears and sees; but the sealed one has no opening by which he can hear or see.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: نور يقذفه الله تعالى في قلب المؤمن فينشرح صدره وينفسح … نعم الإِنابة إلى دار الخلود والتجافي عن دار الغرور والإِستعداد للموت قبل نزول الموت
narrations.chain: in al-Majma, a sound report

text.en: A light God casts into the believer's heart, so his breast expands and widens. Its sign is turning toward the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and readiness for death before death comes.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi
narrations.arabic: كل من والى قوماً فهو منهم وإن لم يكن من جنسهم

text.en: Everyone who allies himself with a people belongs to them, even if he is not of their kind.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما انتصر الله من ظالم إلاّ بظالم وذلك قوله عزّ وجلّ وكذلك نوليّ بعض الظالمين بعضاً
narrations.chain: in al-Kafi and al-Ayyashi, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God never took requital from a wrongdoer except by means of another wrongdoer - and that is His saying, 'That is how We make the wrongdoers one another's friends.'

perspectives.en: On 'whomever He desires to lead astray' in 125, and 'that they may plot' in 123, the traditions divide. Tabrisi holds that God opens the breast as grace and reward for one who accepts guidance, while the straitening is a punishment for refusing faith, not a barring from it [5]; Tusi reads the 'that they may plot' as the lam of consequence, since God does not will their scheming [9]. Al-Razi, by contrast, takes both verses as proof that guidance, misguidance, and the plotting itself run by God's will and decree [53][55].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فإن الله سبحانه ينسب للإِنسان الإِلهي في كلامه حياة خالدة أبدية لا تنقطع بالموت الدنيوي

sources.gloss: God ascribes to the godly person an everlasting life that is not cut off by worldly death.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالقضاء الإِلهي لا يسلب عنهم الاختيار الذي عليه مدار المؤاخذة والمجازاة

sources.gloss: The divine decree does not strip them of the choice on which accountability and requital turn.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إنها عامة في كل مؤمن وكافر عن الحسن وجماعة وهذا أولى لأنه أعمَّ فائدة فيدخل فيه جميع الأقوال المذكورة

sources.gloss: It was said the verse is general, about every believer and disbeliever (al-Hasan and a group); this is preferable because it is more comprehensive and includes all the reported views.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ومن يرد أن يضله عن ثوابه وكرامته يجعل صدره في كفره ضيقاً حرجاً عقوبة له على ترك الإيمان من غير أن يكون سبحانه مانعاً له عن الإيمان وسالباً إياه القدرة عليه

sources.gloss: Whomever He wishes to lead away from His reward, He makes his breast narrow in his disbelief as a punishment for abandoning faith, without His barring him from faith or stripping his power over it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { وهذا صرَاط ربك } أي طريق ربك وهو القرآن عن ابن مسعود والإسلام عن ابن عباس

sources.gloss: 'This is your Lord's path' - the way of your Lord: the Quran (Ibn Masud) or Islam (Ibn Abbas).

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على وجوب طلب العلم، لانه تعالى رغب فيه بأن جعله كالحياة في الادراك بها والنور في الاهتداء به

sources.gloss: The verse indicates the obligation of seeking knowledge, since God commended it by making it like life for perception and light for guidance.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وليس المراد بها لام الغرض، لانه تعالى لا يريد أن يمكروا

sources.gloss: It is not the lam of purpose, for God does not will that they plot.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لان الرسالة تابعة للمصلحة، ولا يبعث الله تعالى الا من يعلم ان مصلحة الخلق تتعلق ببعثه

sources.gloss: Because apostleship follows benefit; God sends only one whom He knows the people's welfare depends upon.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال النور الولاية { كمن مثله في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها } يعني: في ولاية غير الأئمة

sources.gloss: He said: the light is the guardianship; 'like one in a darkness he cannot leave' means being in the guardianship of other than the Imams.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: كل من والى قوماً فهو منهم وإن لم يكن من جنسهم

sources.gloss: Everyone who allies himself with a people belongs to them, even if he is not of their kind.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ميت لا يعرف شيئا { نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ } إماما يأتم به

sources.gloss: Dead, knowing nothing; 'a light by which he walks among people' - an Imam whom he follows.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: نور يقذفه الله تعالى في قلب المؤمن فينشرح صدره وينفسح

sources.gloss: A light God casts into the believer's heart, so his breast expands and widens.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ما انتصر الله من ظالم إلاّ بظالم وذلك قوله عزّ وجلّ وكذلك نوليّ بعض الظالمين بعضاً

sources.gloss: God never took requital from a wrongdoer except by another wrongdoer; and that is His saying, 'That is how We make the wrongdoers one another's friends.'

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: إن الله بعث في كل زمان خيرة ومن كل خيرة منتجباً

sources.gloss: God raised up in every age a chosen group, and from every chosen group a select one.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وذلك يقتضي أنه تعالى إنما جعلهم بهذه الصفة، لأنه أراد منهم أن يمكروا بالناس، فهذا أيضاً يدل على أن الخير والشر بإرادة الله تعالى

sources.gloss: This entails that He made them so because He willed that they plot against people; this too shows that good and evil are by God's will.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: تمسك أصحابنا بهذه الآية في بيان أن الضلال والهداية من الله تعالى

sources.gloss: Our companions rely on this verse to show that misguidance and guidance are from God.

essay.en:
The passage opens on the Day of Resurrection, when God gathers jinn and humans and asks whether messengers had not come to them from among themselves, recounting His signs and warning of the meeting of this Day. Al-Tabrisi reads this as an argument that leaves them no excuse: God had sent them messengers as warning and to make the proof binding [3]. They can only testify against themselves and admit that the life of this world had deceived them. This is why, the next verse says, your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were unaware, for no one is punished before the proof has reached him.

Everyone is then given ranks according to what they did, and nothing they do escapes Him. Your Lord, the passage adds, is the All-sufficient dispenser of mercy: al-Tabrisi explains that He is beyond His servants' deeds, so their obedience does not benefit Him nor their disobedience harm Him [4]. If He willed, He could remove them and bring others in their place, and Tabatabai adds that this decree never strips a person of the free choice on which accountability turns [1].

What is promised will surely come, and they cannot thwart it. The Prophet is then told to say, "act according to your ability; I too am acting," which al-Tusi explains is a threat cast in the form of a command [15]. Soon they will know in whose favour the outcome of that abode falls.

The passage closes with the polytheists' inventions, which Tabatabai frames as a dispute over rulings they had fabricated about food and property [2]. They assigned God a share of the crops and cattle and their idols another; their "partners," in al-Tabrisi's reading the satans, made the killing of their children seem fair [6]; and they declared cattle and crops taboo and reserved the unborn for their males. By attributing the killing and the forbidding to them and clearing Himself of it, al-Tabrisi observes, these verses refute the doctrine of compulsion [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: سأل أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام هل بعث الله نبيّاً إلى الجنّ فقال نعم بعث الله نبيّاً يقال له يوسف فدعاهم إلى الله فقتلوه

text.en: A Syrian man asked the Commander of the Faithful whether God had sent a prophet to the jinn. He said: Yes, God sent a prophet named Yusuf; he called them to God, and they killed him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله عزّ وجلّ أرسل محمّداً صلىّ الله عليه وآله وسلم إلى الجنّ والإِنس

text.en: In a tradition, Imam al-Baqir said that God, mighty and majestic, sent Muhammad to both the jinn and mankind.

note.en: They split their crops and cattle between God and the idols, then favoured the idols: water flowing toward the idols' plot they let run, water toward God's they blocked. Al-Tabrisi reports this from the Imams [5].

Al-Qummi distinguishes two groups here: those who killed daughters out of jealousy and those who killed their children from hunger, and he links the verse to the command against killing children for fear of poverty [29].

perspectives.en: Verse 130 speaks of apostles from yourselves to both jinn and humans, and the traditions divide over whether the jinn had messengers of their own. On the Shia side, Imam Ali's report names a jinn prophet, Yusuf, whom they killed, and al-Tusi holds the view that God sent messengers from the jinn to be the strongest reading [34][10]. Ibn Kathir, representing the dominant Sunni position, holds that messengers came only from humankind and that the jinn had merely warners, who relayed to their people what they had heard from the human prophets [47].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالقضاء الإِلهي لا يسلب عنهم الاختيار الذي عليه مدار المؤاخذة والمجازاة

sources.gloss: The divine decree does not strip them of the free choice on which accountability and recompense turn.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات تحاج المشركين في عدة من الأحكام في الأطعمة وغيرها دائرة بين المشركين وتذكر حكم الله فيها

sources.gloss: These verses dispute with the polytheists over a number of rulings about foods and other things current among them, and state God's ruling on them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: هذا احتجاج عليهم بأن بعث إليهم الرسل إعذاراً وإنذاراً وتأكيداً للحجة عليهم

sources.gloss: This is an argument against them: that He sent them messengers to remove their excuse, to warn, and to confirm the proof against them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: عن أعمال عباده لا تنفعه طاعتهم ولا تضرُّه معصيتهم

sources.gloss: Beyond His servants' deeds: their obedience does not benefit Him, nor their disobedience harm Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإذا تخرق الماء من الذي لله في الذي للأصنام لم يسدّوه وإذا تخرق من الذي للأصنام في الذي لله سدُّوه … وهو المروي عن أئمتنا ع

sources.gloss: When water broke from God's plot into the idols' they did not dam it, but from the idols' into God's they dammed it; and this is narrated from our Imams.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعني الشياطين الذين زيَّنوا لهم قتل البنات وَوَأْدَهُنَّ أحياء خيفة العيلة والفقر والعار

sources.gloss: That is, the satans, who made fair to them the killing of daughters and burying them alive out of fear of want, poverty, and shame.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذه الآيات دلالات على بطلان مذهب المجبرة لأنه سبحانه أضاف القتل والافتراء والتحريم إليهم ونَزّه نفسه عن ذلك

sources.gloss: In these verses are proofs against the doctrine of the Determinists, for He attributed the killing, the fabrication, and the forbidding to them and cleared Himself of it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الضحاك: ذلك يدل على انه تعالى ارسل سلا من الجن. وبه قال الطبري واختاره البلخي أيضا، وهو الاقوى

sources.gloss: Al-Dahhak said this shows that God sent messengers from the jinn; al-Tabari said the same and al-Balkhi chose it too, and it is the strongest view.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهذا وان كان صيغته صيغة الامر فالمراد به التهديد

sources.gloss: Although its form is that of a command, what is meant by it is a threat.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهم قوم يقتلون أولادهم من البنات للغيرة وقوم كانوا يقتلون أولادهم من الجوع … فقال الله: { ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق نحن نرزقكم وإياهم }

sources.gloss: They are a people who kill their daughters out of jealousy, and a people who killed their children out of hunger; and God said: do not kill your children for fear of poverty, We provide for you and for them.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: سأل أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام هل بعث الله نبيّاً إلى الجنّ فقال نعم بعث الله نبيّاً يقال له يوسف فدعاهم إلى الله فقتلوه

sources.gloss: He asked the Commander of the Faithful whether God had sent a prophet to the jinn; he said: Yes, God sent a prophet named Yusuf, who called them to God, and they killed him.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والرسل من الإنس فقط، وليس من الجن رسل … وقال ابن عباس الرسل من بني آدم، ومن الجن نذر

sources.gloss: The messengers are from humankind only, and there are no messengers from the jinn; and Ibn Abbas said: the messengers are from the children of Adam, and from the jinn there are only warners.

essay.en:
The verses just before this exposed how the polytheists carved up their crops and cattle, assigning a share to God and a share to their idols. This passage takes up the argument with them over what they had declared lawful and forbidden [1]. It answers by naming God the Creator of it all: He produces the gardens, trellised and without trellises, the palms and crops 'of diverse produce,' the olives and pomegranates, 'similar and dissimilar.' Because He alone produces these things, none may be handed to idols, nor declared lawful or unlawful except by His leave [2].

The commands that follow are of two kinds. 'Eat of its fruits when it fructifies' grants permission rather than an order [4], while 'give its due on the day of harvest' lays down a duty the narrations make concrete. And 'do not be wasteful,' for He does not like the wasteful.

The passage turns to the cattle, some for burden and some for slaughter. Eat what God has provided, and 'do not follow in Satan's footsteps,' which lead a person from the lawful to the forbidden and back [5]. Then comes the challenge: eight mates, of sheep, goats, camels and oxen. Did God forbid the two males, the two females, or what the wombs contain? 'Inform me with knowledge.' Were they present when God enjoined this? They were not, so no one wrongs himself more than he who fabricates a lie against God to mislead the people. God does not guide such wrongdoers.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الضغث من السنبل، و الكف من التمر، إذا خرص
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Asked about 'and give its due on the day of harvest,' he said: A bunch from the ears of grain and a handful from the dates, once the crop has been estimated.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في الزرع حقان: حق تؤخذ به، و حق تعطيه … أما الذي تؤخذ به فالعشر و نصف العشر
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Shurayh, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: In a crop there are two rights: a right by which you are taxed, and a right that you give. The one by which you are taxed is the tithe and the half-tithe; the one you give is God's word, 'and give its due on the day of harvest.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: حمل نوح (عليه السلام) في السفينة الأزواج الثمانية … فكان من الضأن اثنين: زوج داجنة يربيها الناس، و الزوج الآخر الضأن التي تكون في الجبال الوحشية أحل لهم صيدها
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi and Abd al-Karim ibn Amr and Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Nuh carried in the ark the eight mates that God named. Of the sheep were two: a domestic pair that people raise, and the other the wild mountain sheep, whose hunting was made lawful for them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تعالى أحل في الاضحية بمنى الضأن و المعز الأهلية، و حرم أن يضحى بالجبلية … أحل في الاضحية الإبل العراب، و حرم منها البخاتي، و أحل البقر الأهلية أن يضحى بها، و حرم الجبلية
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from al-Sulami, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God made lawful for the Mina sacrifice the domestic sheep and goats and forbade sacrificing the mountain kinds; He made lawful the Arabian camels and forbade the Bactrian, and made lawful the domestic cattle and forbade the mountain ones.

perspectives.en: Both traditions agree the passage dismantles the polytheists' invented taboos, yet they read 'give its due on the day of harvest' differently. The Shia Imams distinguish two rights in a crop: an obligatory tithe, the ushr or half-ushr taken as zakat, and a separate due given by hand to the poor present at the harvest, treated as a standing charge alongside zakat [11]. Al-Tabari reports the view, from al-Hasan and Anas, that the harvest-due is the obligatory zakat itself [16], while Ibn Kathir reports that others held it to be a right other than that obligatory zakat [20].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: تحاج المشركين في عدة من الأحكام في الأطعمة وغيرها دائرة بين المشركين وتذكر حكم الله فيها

sources.gloss: [These verses] dispute with the polytheists over a number of rulings concerning foods and other matters current among them, and set out God's ruling on them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فلا يجوز إضافة شيء منها الى الأوثان ولا تحليل ذلك ولا تحريمه إلا بإذنه

sources.gloss: So nothing of them may be attributed to the idols, nor may that be made lawful or unlawful except by His leave.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: المراد به الاباحة لا الامر

sources.gloss: What is meant [by 'eat of its fruits'] is permission, not a command.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ما يتخطى بكم الشيطان اليه من تحليل الى تحريم، ومن تحريم الى تحليل

sources.gloss: What Satan steps you along toward, from making lawful to forbidding, and from forbidding to making lawful.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: في الزرع حقان: حق تؤخذ به، و حق تعطيه

sources.gloss: In a crop there are two rights: a right by which you are taxed, and a right that you give.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أحل في الاضحية بمنى الضأن و المعز الأهلية، و حرم أن يضحى بالجبلية
