sources.gloss: He made lawful for the Mina sacrifice the domestic sheep and goats, and forbade sacrificing the mountain ones.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: هذا أمر من الله بإيتاء الصدقة المفروضة من الثمر والحبّ

sources.gloss: This is a command from God to render the obligatory charity from the fruit and the grain.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وقال آخرون وهو حق آخر سوى الزكاة

sources.gloss: Others said it is a right other than the [obligatory] zakat.

title.en: Forbidden foods and the pagans' plea

essay.en: This passage closes the surah's long dispute with the pagans over which foods may be eaten and which are forbidden [1]. The Prophet is told to say that he finds in what is revealed to him nothing forbidden to an eater except four things: carrion, spilt blood, the flesh of swine, which is unclean, and what is offered to other than God. Tabrisi notes that blood is named as spilt because blood that clings to the meat and cannot be separated is pardoned [2], and that this Meccan surah names only these, while further prohibitions came later in Madinan al-Maida [2]. On the one compelled who is not rebellious, Tusi records that the Imams' followers read the rebel as one who rises against a just imam [5]. The passage then turns to the Jews, to whom God forbade certain animals and the fat of oxen and sheep as a requital for their rebelliousness [6]; Qummi explains that their kings kept the poor from bird-meat and fat, so God forbade these to them [12]. Last comes the pagans' fatalist plea: 'Had Allah wished we would not have ascribed any partner [to Him], nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything.' Tusi treats these words as the clearest proof that God does not will unbelief, against those who trace sin to His will [8]. To Allah belongs the conclusive argument [9], and He calls for witnesses they can never produce [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لم يحرم الله تعالى شيئا من الحيوان في القرآن إلا الخنزير بعينه، و يكره كل شيء من البحر ليس له قشر مثل الورق، و ليس بحرام و إنما هو مكروه
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh, by his chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God has forbidden no animal in the Quran by name except swine. Everything from the sea that has no scale like a leaf is disliked, but it is not forbidden; it is only disliked.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا محمد، اقرأ هذه الآية التي في الأنعام … إنما الحرام ما حرم الله و رسوله في كتابه، و لكنهم قد كانوا يعافون أشياء فنحن نعافها
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Muhammad, read this verse in al-An'am. The forbidden is only what God and His Messenger forbade in His book; but they used to shun certain things, so we too shun them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: حرم على بني إسرائيل كل ذي ظفر و الشحوم إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Forbidden to the Children of Israel was every animal with claws, and the fats, except what their backs bore, or the entrails, or what was mixed with a bone.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك و تعالى يقول للعبد يوم القيامة: عبدي أ كنت عالما؟ فإن قال: نعم، قال له: أ فلا عملت بما علمت؟ و إن قال: كنت جاهلا، قال له: أ فلا تعلمت حتى تعمل، فيخصمه، فتلك الحجة البالغة
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh in his Amali, from al-Mufid, from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Himyari, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad

text.en: On the Day of Resurrection God asks the servant, 'Were you knowing?' If he says yes, He says, 'Then why did you not act on what you knew?' If he says he was ignorant, He says, 'Why did you not learn, so you could act?' So He silences him. That is the conclusive argument.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نحن الحجة البالغة على من دون السماء و فوق الأرض
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Husayn, from Abu Talib al-Qummi, from Sadir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: We are the conclusive argument over all that is beneath the sky and above the earth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: إن لله على الناس حجتين حجة ظاهرة وحجة باطنة فأما الظاهرة فالرسل والأنبياء والأئمّة امّا الباطنة فالعقول
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi, from al-Kazim

text.en: God has two proofs over people: an outward proof and an inward one. The outward are the messengers, the prophets and the imams; the inward are the intellects.

perspectives.en: The pagans' plea, 'Had Allah wished we would not have ascribed partners,' divides the readings on divine will. Tusi treats the verse as the clearest proof that God does not will disobedience or unbelief, and reads its rebuke of the plea as a rejection of those who trace sin to God's will [8]. Ibn Kathir, on the same verses, holds that guidance and misguidance alike proceed by God's power, will and choice, while He is pleased with the believers and detests the disbelievers; the plea fails not because God did not will their state but because His conclusive argument still stands [30].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: تحاج المشركين في عدة من الأحكام في الأطعمة وغيرها دائرة بين المشركين وتذكر حكم الله فيها

sources.gloss: The verses dispute with the polytheists over several rulings concerning foods and other matters current between them, and state God's ruling on them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإنما خصَّ المصبوب بالذكر لأن ما يختلط باللحم منه مما لا يمكن تخليصه منه معفوٌّ عنه مباح … وأيضاً فإن هذه السورة مكية والمائدة مدنية

sources.gloss: The spilt blood is singled out because blood that mixes with the meat and cannot be separated from it is pardoned and permitted; and this surah is Meccan while al-Maida is Madinan.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وروى أصحابنا في قوله { غير باغ } ان معناه ان لا يكون خارجا على إِمام عادل

sources.gloss: Our companions related regarding 'without being rebellious' that it means he should not be one who rebels against a just imam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله { ذلك جزيناهم ببغيهم } معناه انا حرمنا ذلك عليهم عقوبة لهم على بغيهم

sources.gloss: 'That We requited them for their rebelliousness' means We forbade it to them as a punishment for their rebelliousness.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفى هذه الآية أدلُّ دلالة على ان الله تعالى لا يشاء المعاصي والكفر

sources.gloss: In this verse is the clearest proof that God does not will acts of disobedience and unbelief.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى { البالغة } التي تبلغ قطع عذر المحجوج وتزيل كل لبس وشبهة عمن نظر فيها

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'conclusive' is that which reaches the point of cutting off the excuse of the one argued against and removes every ambiguity and doubt from whoever considers it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: امر الله تعالى نبيه (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ان يقول لهؤلاء الكفار الذين تقدم وصفهم " هلموا " ومعناه هاتوا

sources.gloss: God commanded His Prophet to say to these disbelievers already described, 'Come forward' - meaning, produce your witnesses.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: إنه كان ملوك بني إسرائيل يمنعون فقراء‌هم من أكل لحم الطير والشحوم فحرم الله ذلك عليهم ببغيهم على فقراء‌هم

sources.gloss: The kings of the Children of Israel used to keep their poor from eating bird-meat and fats, so God forbade that to them for their wronging their poor.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لم يحرم الله تعالى شيئا من الحيوان في القرآن إلا الخنزير بعينه … إنما الحرام ما حرم الله و رسوله في كتابه

sources.gloss: God has forbidden no animal in the Quran by name except swine ... The forbidden is only what God and His Messenger forbade in His book.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فيخصمه، فتلك الحجة البالغة … نحن الحجة البالغة على من دون السماء و فوق الأرض

sources.gloss: So He silences him, and that is the conclusive argument ... We are the conclusive argument over all beneath the sky and above the earth.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: إن لله على الناس حجتين حجة ظاهرة وحجة باطنة فأما الظاهرة فالرسل والأنبياء والأئمّة امّا الباطنة فالعقول

sources.gloss: God has two proofs over people: an outward proof and an inward one; the outward are the messengers, prophets and imams, and the inward are the intellects.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: فكل ذلك بقدرته ومشيئته واختياره، وهو مع ذلك يرضى عن المؤمنين، ويبغض الكافرين

sources.gloss: All of that is by His power, will and choice, yet He is pleased with the believers and detests the disbelievers.

essay.en:
Set against people who forbade what God never forbade and permitted what He did forbid, the passage answers with what He truly enjoins: 'Say, Come, I will recount what your Lord has forbidden you' [5]. Tabatabai reads the list that follows as the prohibitions common to every divine law and particular to none - ascribing partners to God, failing the parents, killing children out of poverty, approaching indecencies, wronging the orphan, and cheating the measure [1]. Ascribing partners stands first, he notes, because it is the great wrong for which no divine forgiveness is hoped [1]. Each group closes with the same refrain, 'This is what He has enjoined upon you,' sealed in turn with reason, remembrance, and Godwariness.

On the orphan, Majma al-Bayan explains that 'approach' means handling the property, and that the orphan is singled out because he can defend neither himself nor his wealth [3]. Verse 153 then gathers the whole into a single line: 'This indeed is my straight path, so follow it, and do not follow other ways.' Al-Tusi names the obligatory and the forbidden a 'path' because keeping to it leads to Paradise, and reads the 'other ways' as the ways of Satan and of the sects that break from it [7]. The Book given to Moses is then called a completion for his virtue and 'an elaboration of all things' [4] - verses the Imams called muhkam, and never abrogated [16].

note.en: Al-Qummi glosses 'the parents' here as the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, giving the charge to honor parents an inner sense as well [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: انه كان متكئاً على فراشه اذ قرء الآيات المحكمات التي لم ينسخهن شيء من الأنعام فقال شيّعهن سبعون ألف ملك
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He was reclining on his couch when he recited the clear verses of al-An'am that nothing has abrogated, and said: seventy thousand angels escorted them down.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sajjad
narrations.arabic: ما ظهر نكاح امرأة الأب وما بطن الزنا
narrations.chain: al-Kafi and al-Ayyashi, from al-Sajjad

text.en: The outward indecency is marrying the father's wife, and the inward is fornication.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما ظهر هو الزّنا وما بطن المخالة
narrations.chain: Majma al-Bayan, from al-Baqir

text.en: The outward is fornication, and the inward is the taking of a secret lover.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: انقطاع يُتْم اليتيم الاحتلام وهو اشدّه وان احتلم ولم يونس منه رشده وكان سفيهاً أو ضعيفاً فليمسك عنه وليّه ماله
narrations.chain: al-Faqih and al-Tahdhib, from al-Sadiq

text.en: The end of an orphan's orphanhood is puberty, which is his coming of age. Yet if he reaches puberty and no sound judgment is seen in him, being foolish or weak, his guardian withholds his property from him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نحن السبيل فمن أبى فهذه السبل فقد كفر
narrations.chain: al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: We are the way; whoever refuses it - these are the other ways - has disbelieved.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: أنا الصراط المستقيم الذي آمركم باتباعه ثمّ عليّ من بعدي ثم ولدي من صلبه أئمّة يهدون بالحقّ وبه يعدلون
narrations.chain: al-Ihtijaj, from the Prophet's Ghadir sermon

text.en: I am the straight path whose following I command you, then Ali after me, then my descendants from his loins, Imams who guide by the truth and by it act with justice.

perspectives.en: Both traditions treat these verses as a foundational, unabrogated charter: Qurtubi records Ibn Abbas calling them the muhkam verses on which every people's law agrees, never abrogated in any religion, and Kab placing them at the head of the Torah [26]. They part over verse 153. Sunni exegetes gloss the 'other ways' as innovations and misguided sects [20], citing Ibn Masud's report that the Prophet drew one line as God's straight path and lines beside it, each with a devil calling to it [24]. Shia narrations identify the path itself with the Imam: al-Baqir taught that he and the Imams are God's straight path, and that whoever refuses it has disbelieved [11][17].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الآيات المحرمات العامة التي لا تختص بشريعة من الشرائع الإِلهية

sources.gloss: These are the verses of prohibition that are common to all the divine laws and particular to none.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: المراد بالقرب التصرف فيه وإنما خص مال اليتيم بالذكر لأَنه لا يستطيع الدفاع عن نفسه ولا عن ماله

sources.gloss: 'Approaching' means handling the property; the orphan's is singled out because he can defend neither himself nor his wealth.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: تماماً على إحسان موسى فكأنه قال ليكمل إحسانه الذي يستحق به كمال ثوابه في الآخرة

sources.gloss: A completion upon Moses' virtue, as if to perfect the virtue by which he merits the fullness of his reward in the Hereafter.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: حرموا ما لم يحرمه الله

sources.gloss: These people forbade what God did not forbid.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يعني سبل الشيطان واتباع اهل البدع من اليهود والنصارى وغيرهم

sources.gloss: The 'other ways' mean the ways of Satan and the following of the innovators among the Jews, Christians and others.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الوالدين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وأمير المؤمنين صلوات الله عليه

sources.gloss: 'The parents' are the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الصراط المستقيم الإِمام فاتبعوه

sources.gloss: The straight path is the Imam, so follow it.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ما ظهر نكاح امرأة الأب وما بطن الزنا

sources.gloss: The outward indecency is marrying the father's wife, and the inward is fornication.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: الآيات المحكمات التي لم ينسخهن شيء من الأنعام فقال شيّعهن سبعون ألف ملك

sources.gloss: The clear verses of al-An'am that nothing has abrogated; he said that seventy thousand angels escorted them.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: نحن صراطه المستقيم فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل

sources.gloss: We are His straight path, so follow it, and do not follow the other ways.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: فإنها بدع وضلالات

sources.gloss: For these are innovations and misguidances.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: هذا سبيل الله مستقيماً … هذه السبل ليس منها سبيل إلا عليه شيطان يدعو إليه

sources.gloss: This is God's path, made straight; these are the other ways, upon each of which is a devil calling to it.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: أجمعت عليها شرائع الخلق، ولم تنسخ قط في مِلّة

sources.gloss: The laws of all creation agree upon these verses, and they were never abrogated in any religion.

essay.en:
The surah closes by turning from the forbidden things just listed to the scripture that carries them: this Book, sent down and blessed [11], is to be followed in Godwariness so that mercy may come. It was sent, the next verses explain, to close every excuse - that the Arabs might not plead that scripture had gone only to two communities before them, the Jews and the Christians [12], or claim that, had it reached them, they would have been better guided. Now a clear proof, a guidance and a mercy has come [13], and no one wrongs himself more than one who denies God's signs and turns from them.

What, then, do the deniers await? al-Mizan reads the warning of verse 158 as a promise of judgment: the angels' coming means their descent with the punishment [2], while the day a sign arrives is the day faith no longer benefits a soul that had not believed before. Commentators name that sign the sun rising from its place of setting [6]. Those who tear their religion into sects the Prophet is told to disown, their affair resting with God alone. Against their fracture stands God's generosity: a good deed is repaid tenfold, an evil one only in kind, out of His immense grace [8].

The surah ends on the Prophet's own confession. He is told to declare that his Lord has guided him to a straight path, the upright religion, the creed of Abraham the Hanif, and that his prayer and worship, his life and his death, belong to God alone, who has no partner. al-Mizan notes that a mark of truthfulness is that a man act on what he preaches [3]. He seeks no Lord besides the Lord of all things; no soul earns but against itself [19], and no bearer bears another's burden. God made you successors on the earth [20], raising some above others to test you - swift in retribution, yet all-forgiving, all-merciful.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنّ سورة الأنعام نزلت جملة واحدة شيّعها سبعون ألف ملك حتى نزلت على محمّد صلىّ الله عليه وآله وسلم فعظّموها وبجّلوها فانّ اسم الله فيها في سبعين موضعاً ولو يعلم الناس ما في قراءتها ما تركوها

text.en: Surat al-An'am was sent down all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, until it came down upon Muhammad. So magnify it and honour it, for God's name occurs in it in seventy places; if people knew what its recitation holds, they would never abandon it.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أو يأتي ربّك أو يأتي بعض آيات ربك يعني بذلك أمر ربّك والآيات هي العذاب في دار الدنيا كما عذب الأمم السالفة والقرون الخالية

text.en: By 'or your Lord may come' He means the command of your Lord; and the signs are the punishment in this world, as He punished the earlier communities and the bygone generations.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الآيات: الأئمة، و الآية المنتظرة: القائم (عليه السلام)، فيومئذ لا ينفع نفسا إيمانها لم تكن آمنت من قبل قيامه بالسيف، و إن آمنت بمن تقدم من آبائه (عليهم السلام)
narrations.chain: al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The signs are the Imams, and the awaited sign is the Qa'im. On that day faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before his rising with the sword, even if it had believed in his forefathers who came before.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كان علي يقرأها: فارقوا دينهم … فارق و الله القوم دينهم
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Kulayb al-Saydawi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Ali used to read it 'faraqu dinahum' - they parted from their religion. By God, the people parted from their religion.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الحسنة الستر والسيئة إذاعة حديثنا
narrations.chain: al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The good deed is concealment, and the evil deed is broadcasting our hadith.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال آدم يا ربّ سلطته على ولدي وأجريته فيهم مجرى الدّم في العروق وأعطيته ما أعطيتّه فما لي ولولدي فقال لك ولولدك السّيئة بواحدة والحسنة بعشر أمثالها … قال التوبة مبسوطة الى أن تبلغ النّفس الحلقوم فقال يا ربّ زدني قال اغفر ولا أبالي

text.en: Adam said: 'Lord, You set Iblis over my children and made him course through them like blood. What is left for me and mine?' He said: 'For you and your children, an evil deed counts as one and a good deed as tenfold; repentance stays open until the soul reaches the throat; I forgive and do not mind.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما أبقت الحنيفية شيئا، حتى أن منها قص الأظفار، و أخذ الشارب، و الختان
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The upright creed of Abraham left nothing out - even trimming the nails, taking the moustache, and circumcision are part of it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: صدق الله في جميع أقواله ولكن ذراري قتلة الحسين عليه السلام يرضون بفعال آبائهم ويفتخرون بها ومن رضي شيئاً كان كمن أتاه ولو أنّ رجلاً قتل بالمشرق فرضي بقتله رجل في المغرب لكان الراضي عند الله شريك القاتل

text.en: God speaks truly in all He says. But the descendants of Husayn's killers are pleased with what their fathers did and boast of it, and whoever is pleased with a deed is like one who did it. Were a man killed in the east and another in the west pleased with it, that man would share the killer's guilt.

perspectives.en: The heaviest divergence falls on 'those who split up their religion and became sects' in verse 159. Sunni exegetes read it chiefly of the Jews and the Christians, who differed and broke into parties before the Prophet's mission [47], and, more broadly, of everyone who parts from God's religion and opposes it, across creeds and sects [56]. Qummi, reading the word as 'faraqu' - they parted - glosses the sect-makers as those who parted from Amir al-Mu'minin and became factions [25]. Both traditions condemn sectarian rupture; they differ over whom the verse names.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولازم هذا السياق أن يكون المراد بإتيان الملائكة نزولهم بآية العذاب

sources.gloss: The context requires that the angels' coming means their descent with the sign of punishment.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فإن من إمارة الصدق أن يعمل الإِنسان بما يندب إليه، ويطابق فعله قوله

sources.gloss: A mark of truthfulness is that a person acts on what he calls others to, his deed matching his word.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وذلك نحو خروج الدابة أو طلوع الشمس من مغربها عن مجاهد وقتادة والسدي

sources.gloss: That is, such as the emergence of the Beast or the sun rising from its place of setting - from Mujahid, Qatada and al-Suddi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وذلك من عظيم فضل الله تعالى وجزيل إنعامه على عباده حيث لا يقتصر في الثواب على قدر الاستحقاق بل يزيد عليه

sources.gloss: This is from God's immense grace and lavish favour to His servants: He does not limit the reward to what is merited but increases it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فالبركة ثبوت الخير بزيادته ونموه

sources.gloss: Baraka is the establishment of good together with its increase and growth.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انما أنزل الكتاب على اليهود والنصارى، ولم ينزل علينا

sources.gloss: The Book was sent down only to the Jews and the Christians, and not to us.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يعني حجة واضحة { وهدى ورحمة } وادلة مؤدية الى الحق، ورحمة منه تعالى وانعام

sources.gloss: That is, a clear proof - 'and a guidance and mercy' - and evidences leading to the truth, and a mercy and favour from Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معناه لا يكون جزاء عمل كل نفس الا عليها

sources.gloss: It means the recompense of each soul's deed falls only upon it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ان كل اهل عصر يخلفون اهل العصر الذي قبله

sources.gloss: Each generation succeeds the generation before it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فارقوا أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام وصاروا أحزاباً

sources.gloss: They parted from Amir al-Mu'minin and became parties.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الآيات: الأئمة، و الآية المنتظرة: القائم (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: The signs are the Imams, and the awaited sign is the Qa'im.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كان علي يقرأها: فارقوا دينهم

sources.gloss: Ali used to read it 'faraqu dinahum' - they parted from their religion.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما أبقت الحنيفية شيئا، حتى أن منها قص الأظفار، و أخذ الشارب، و الختان

sources.gloss: The upright creed left nothing out - even trimming the nails, taking the moustache, and circumcision are part of it.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: يعني بذلك أمر ربّك والآيات هي العذاب في دار الدنيا

sources.gloss: By 'your Lord may come' He means the command of your Lord, and the signs are the punishment in this world.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لك ولولدك السّيئة بواحدة والحسنة بعشر أمثالها

sources.gloss: For you and your children, an evil deed counts as one and a good deed as tenfold.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: من رضي شيئاً كان كمن أتاه

sources.gloss: Whoever is pleased with a deed is like one who did it.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنّ سورة الأنعام نزلت جملة واحدة شيّعها سبعون ألف ملك

sources.gloss: Surat al-An'am was sent down all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: الحسنة الستر والسيئة إذاعة حديثنا

sources.gloss: The good deed is concealment, and the evil deed is divulging our hadith.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وذلك أن اليهود والنصارى اختلفوا قبل أن يبعث محمد فتفرّقوا

sources.gloss: That is because the Jews and the Christians differed before Muhammad was sent and split into parties.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: والظاهر أن الآية عامة في كل من فارق دين الله، وكان مخالفاً له … أي فرقاً كأهل الملل والنحل والأهواء والضلالات

sources.gloss: The apparent meaning is that the verse is general, covering everyone who parts from God's religion and opposes it … that is, factions like the people of creeds and sects, desires and errors.
